title: 7K20--VA East Indianapolis PAR Excellence Weight Based Inventory Management System Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation
description: Page 2 of 2 Department of Veterans Affairs Veteran Health Indiana, East Indianapolis VA Clinic for PAR Excellence Weight Based Inventory Management System Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Request for Information 36C10B24Q0140 Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for conducting market research and planning purposes only. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote, Request for Proposal, nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. Additionally, this RFI does not restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who can meet Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for a brand name PAR Excellence Weight Based Inventory Management System. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI. Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. Background: The VA is considering an effort brand name PAR Excellence (PAR) Weight-based Inventory Management Systems (WBIMS) for the Veteran Health Indiana, East Indianapolis VA Clinic. The VA anticipates a need for an automated inventory system for a medical setting that tracks supply quantities by weight, detecting when items are removed because the weight of their storage container changes. Please see the attached Draft Product Description (PD) for more information on the request. RFI Response Instructions: All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information: NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI. Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed. Interested Vendors shall at a minimum provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission (note acronyms used in the table are defined below the table): Name of Company: Address: Point of Contact: Phone Number: Email Address: Company Business Size & Status: For VOSB and SDVOSBs, proof of certification with SBA: NAICS code(s): Socioeconomic Data: If a small business, please identify socio-economic category(ies). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS or MAC): The RFI source and RFI # you are responding to: *� If you believe there is a more appropriate NAICS code, please provide that to the Government with your rationale. Acronyms: FSS - Federal Supply Schedule, GWAC - Government-wide Acquisition Contract NAICS North American Industry Classification NASA SEWP - National Aeronautics and Space Administration Solutions for Enterprise Wide Procurement SBA Small Business Administration SDVOSB Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business VOSB Veteran-Owned Small Business For SDVOSB / VOSB concerns, indicate whether at least 50 percent of the cost of performance incurred is planned to be expended for employees of your concern or employees of other eligible SDVOSB/VOSB concerns. Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible.� Brief summary (not to exceed 5 pages), describing your company s technical approach to meeting the requirements outlined below. 1. What brand and/or solution does your company offer that is capable of meeting this requirement? 2. Does your system track inventory by weight? For example, if a bandaid was removed would the system know and show a change in the total number of bandaids? The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Veteran Health Indiana East Indianapolis VA Clinic (Indy East) has a requirement for Brand Name PAR Excellence Weight Based Inventory Management Systems (WBIM) and associated components as described herein. This requirement supports the initial outfitting, transition, and activation (IOT&A) efforts of the Indy East clinic. Responses to this RFI shall be submitted electronically no later than 11:00 AM Eastern Standard Time, December 1, 2026, via email to the Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) points of contact: Joshua Lemonds, Contract Specialist, Joshua.Lemonds@va.gov; and Diana Armesto, Contracting Officer, Diana.Armesto@va.gov Please note Weight Based Inventory Management System in the subject line of your response. Mark your response as Proprietary Information if the information is considered business sensitive. All proprietary/company confidential material shall be clearly marked on every page that contains such. The email file size shall not exceed 5 MB. RESPONDENTS ARE ADVISED THAT THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE DELAYED, CANCELED, OR REVISED AT ANY TIME.

title: S205--FY27 Solid Waste Collection Services
description: SOLICITATION DESCRIPTION The VA Caribbean Healthcare System (VACHS), 10 Casia St, San Juan, PR 00921, has a requirement for Solid Waste Collection Services. Services will include solid waste and recyclable waste collection services at various locations of the VACHS, to include the main facility at San Juan, PR, its Carolina Warehouse, and its Mayaguez Out-patient Clinic (MOPC). Collection services include four (4) electric compactors (three at VACHS and one at MOPC), in addition to four open-top dumpsters at VACHS, and two open-top dumpsters at the Carolina Warehouse. The Contractor shall have the resources necessary for the provision these services. Waste Collection services include the collection of Recyclable Waste, which is composed of wooden pallets, aluminum, plastic, and vegetative waste. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 62111 (Solid Waste Collection), and the Product Service Code (PSC) is S205 (Housekeeping Trash/Garbage Collection). Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Quoter whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate quotes: 1. Technical Capability: The technical submission will primarily determine the qualifications and capability of the quoter to participate in this contract. It should be specific and complete in every detail. The submission should be concise and provide sufficient information to demonstrate the quoter s capacity to satisfactory perform the task(s) outlined in the solicitation. Content of technical submission - The technical submission shall include at a minimum: i. A technical approach that details how the requirements of the PWS will be accomplished. ii. Sufficient documentation (including brochures, pamphlets, product literature, etc.), to allow thorough evaluation of the quote. iii. Demonstrate the ability to meet the requirements in the solicitation as stated in the PWS. iv. Vendor must also submit the following: - License to transport and dispose of Solid Waste in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, provided by the Puerto Rico Department of Natural Resources. - Permit to dispose of Solid Waste in Puerto Rico landfills. - Department of Transportation (DOT) permit for vehicles transporting Solid Waste. 2. Past Performance: The past performance submissions will primarily determine the competency of the quoter s historical performance, and how that competency can be employed to predict the quoter s success in performing the task(s) listed in the solicitation. Content of Past Performance Submittal - The past performance shall include at a minimum: i. A list of Points of Contact (POCs) for two current or previous contracts and/or agreements you have with other public or private firms for the type of work included in this solicitation. ii. This information should include name, email address, and telephone number. 3. Price: The pricing submission will primarily inform the Government as to the prices the vendor can perform the work in accordance with the solicitation. Questions submission shall be received not later than 12:00 PM Atlantic Standard Time (AST) on November 20, 2026 at wilfredo.perez3@va.gov. Submission of your response shall be received not later than 12:00 PM AST on December 1, 2026 at wilfredo.perez3@va.gov. The quoter shall submit a PDF version of the quote to the Government. Late submissions shall be treated in accordance with the solicitation provision at FAR 52.212-1(c). Omission of any one item MAY result in a quoter package being deemed not technically acceptable. Basis for Award. The Government will issue a contract to the responsible quoter whose quotation conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered.

description: Danės upės Klaipėdos miesto savivaldybės teritorijoje valymo, gilinimo ir tvarkymo darbų projekto parengimo paslaugų pirkimo RINKOS KONSULTACIJA. Rinkos konsultacija skelbiama iki pirkimo pradžios. Rinkos konsultacija nėra skelbimas apie pirkimą ar išankstinis skelbimas apie pirkimą. Šios rinkos konsultacijos paskelbimu dalyviai nėra kviečiami varžytis dėl pirkimo sutarties. Dalyvavimas rinkos konsultacijoje yra neatlygintinas, nesuteikiantis pirmenybinio statuso dalyvaujant pirkime. Jokios išlaidos dalyviams neatlyginamos, kompensacijos nemokamos, dalyvavimas rinkos konsultacijoje neturi įtakos ir nesuteikia dalyviui pirmenybės viešiesiems pirkimams, kurie bus skelbiami ateityje, ar jų rezultatams. Rinkos konsultacijos tikslas - informuoti tiekėjus apie planuojamą pirkimą, išsiaiškinti įvairius su pirkimo objektu susijusius klausimus, pasiruošti pirkimui įvertinant pateiktus dokumentus.

title: Conversion & Commercial Fit-Out of 90 Hermon Hill E18 to 105-Place Nursery - HW/4699
description: Happywoods Nursery is seeking an experienced commercial main contractor to undertake the full internal conversion, refurbishment, and fit-out of 90 Hermon Hill, South Woodford, London, E18 1QB, converting a vacant former care home into a 105-place children's day nursery with top-floor administrative offices. Scope & Design Specification Summary (per Dovetail Architects Design Brief Rev 0 & Drawings PL-100 to PL-122): - Classrooms (Babies, Toddlers & 3-5 Years): Forbo welded non-slip vinyl with matching cap & cove; 3mm plaster skim with Dulux Matt Emulsion; Rockfon Blanka dB35 suspended ceilings (600x600mm grid); veneered fire doors with vision panels, finger guards, closers/back-checks & kick plates; adult/child-height handleless base units, 28mm square-edge worktops (mason's mitre), 400mm WhiteRoc splashbacks & SS 1.5 bowl sinks. - WCs & Nappy Change: Forbo welded vinyl; 1200mm WhiteRoc wall panelling; 18mm HPL IPS enclosures & 1100mm cubicles; Armitage Shanks Contour 21 Splash WCs (305/355mm); Franke Wave trough sinks with Avon 21 self-closing taps; Concept Arc 55cm basins; full DDA sanitary packs. - First Floor Commercial Kitchen & Laundry: Full-height WhiteRoc wall panelling; handleless units; min. 2 sinks plus hand-rinse basin; 304 food-grade fully welded SS extraction canopy with baffle filters, LED lights & speed-controlled fan; dedicated AC heating/cooling. - Stair Cores, Offices & Staff Room: Forbo carpet tiles with 150x18mm single-groove MDF skirting; contrasting stair nosings; dual-height brushed 304 SS handrails; 10mm toughened clear glass balustrades; perimeter dado trunking at 850mm FFL; staff kitchenette with microwave housing & 400mm WhiteRoc splashback. - MEP & Security: Central boiler serving Low Surface Temperature (LST) radiators throughout, supplemented by air conditioning units in classrooms, offices & kitchen/laundry; L1 fire alarm & secure video intercom. - Acoustic & External Works (per Clear Acoustic Design Report CAD-26116): Continuous 2.0m absorptive acoustic timber boundary fencing (Jackson's Jakoustic or approved equal, min. 15 kg/m2 surface mass with sealed base junctions); acoustic sealing/lining to party wall adjoining 92 Hermon Hill; Falcon Way drop-off & external play surfacing. Contract & Site Terms: - Form of Contract: JCT Intermediate Building Contract with Contractor's Design (ICD) or JCT Minor Works with Contractor's Design. - Site Possession & DBS Exemption: The property is vacant and unoccupied; full site possession transfers to the Principal Contractor under CDM 2015. Because no children are on site during works, Enhanced DBS clearance is NOT required. Additional information: Site Access, Logistics & Key Notes for Tendering Contractors: Accompanied Site Visits: Site inspections at 90 Hermon Hill (E18 1QB) are strictly by prior appointment during the tender period. Contractors are strongly encouraged to inspect existing M&E incoming capacities, structural layouts, party-wall conditions, and external garden levels prior to submitting pricing. Traffic, Deliveries & Neighbour Amenity: The site sits at the junction of Hermon Hill and Falcon Way, directly adjoining residential properties (including 92 Hermon Hill and Osprey Close). Contractors must factor in a practical Traffic & Logistics Management Plan covering material deliveries, skip positioning, and strict adherence to London Borough of Redbridge permitted construction working hours. Design Brief & Acoustic Compliance: Tenderers must price strictly in accordance with the attached HappyWoods Design Brief (June 2026, Rev 0) and Clear Acoustic Design Noise Impact Assessment (CAD-26116)-specifically the continuous 2.0m absorptive acoustic timber fencing (minimum 15 kg/m² surface mass with sealed base junctions) and party-wall soundproofing specifications. Unoccupied Site / DBS Exemption: The building is vacant and unoccupied; full site possession will transfer to the Principal Contractor under CDM Regulations 2015. Enhanced DBS clearance is NOT required for construction operatives. Clarifications (RFIs): All technical or commercial queries during the tender period must be submitted through this portal's messaging function so anonymized responses can be issued simultaneously to all bidders.

title: Runswick Bay Public wifi design and install
description: To deliver a reliable, free and easy-to-use public Wi-Fi network for Runswick Bay that improves the visitor experience and overall connectivity, provides useful visitor data, while respecting the character of the village and the special qualities of the National Park. The following outputs are mandatory requirements for this brief: 1: A fully installed and operational network by June 2027. 2: Free, legally compliant access (Digital Economy Act 2010, content filtering, UK GDPR). 3: Remote monitoring, maintenance and support for the three-year term. 4: Visitor analytics reporting. The contract will run for three years from the date the network is fully installed and operational.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Bismark, ND
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Bismark, ND area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. Place of Performance The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Bismark, ND. Interested parties must be located no more than 50 miles from the Bismark, ND area. Period of Performance On or about October 1, 2026 � September 30, 2030 (Base plus 3 option years) 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales

NOTE: OFFERORS MUST COMPLETE THE ATTACHED PROVISIONS 52.204-24, 52.204-26, 252.204-7016, AND 252.204-7019AND INCLUDE THE COMPLETED PROVISIONS WITH THEIR OFFER. title: EESC Leetown Science Center (LSC) Propane IDIQ
description: The USGS Eastern Ecological Science Center (EESC) located in Kearneysville, WV has an ongoing requirement for liquid propane gas to be delivered via automatic fill-up on a weekly basis to the following Government-owned tanks. It is anticipated that a single-award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded in response to this solicitation in accordance with FAR Part 12.201-1 Simplified Procedures. Task Orders will be issued on a firm-fixed price basis for various analyses under this contract. The not-to-exceed ceiling for this IDIQ contract is $499,999.00 over a period of performance not-to-exceed four years. This is a 100% small business set-aside. RFQ 140GG027Q0027 will be issued on or about 11/24/2026 with written quotes due on 12/01/2026. The NAICS code is 324110 Petroleum Refineries. The size standard is 1,500 employees. A vendor must be registered at https://sam.gov/SAM/ to receive an award. All responsible sources may submit a response which shall be considered by the agency. These shall be submitted to Dayna Parkin at dayna_parkin@ios.doi.gov.

description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI): Federal Occupational Health � Medications, Vaccines, and Medical Supplies (MVMS) The Government is issuing a Request for Information (RFI) and seeking industry feedback regarding the previous solicitations identified above. The previous solicitation (attached as Draft Solicitation) did not generate the level of industry response and/or proposal quality anticipated by the Government. Accordingly, the Government is interested in engaging with industry to better understand potential factors that may have affected vendor participation and the quality of submissions received. The Government is seeking candid feedback to identify potential improvements to the acquisition strategy and future solicitation requirements. title: STANDARD LABOR DATA COLLECTION AND SITRIBUTION APPLICATION (SLDCADA) DRAFT REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL
description: PAE Mission Systems is soliciting proposals from the eligible SeaPort-NxG small-business contract holders for end-to-end sustainment and infrastructure support of the Standard Labor Data Collection and Distribution Application (SLDCADA). SLDCADA is an unclassified, web-based Government Off-the-Shelf time-and-attendance and labor-reporting information technology application that supports a large Navy, Marine Corps, and Executive Office of the President user community and directly supports payroll and labor-distribution operations. SLDCADA provides a single input screen via a single sign on capability utilizing Common Access Card/Public Key Infrastructure (CAC/PKI)-based login functionality. SLDCADA currently provides T&A capabilities and labor reporting services to more than 60,000 users. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) task order with a one-year base award and four one-year option periods.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Helena, MT
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. Place of Performance The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT. Interested parties must be located no more than 50 miles from the Helena, MT area. Period of Performance On or about October 1, 2026 � September 30, 2026 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. Completed offers must be delivered via email to HAX-BusinessOffice-S@bop.gov. (backup email for bids is cehall@bop.gov . A confirmation email will be sent when bids are received. title: SNOMED CT and Related Services
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 75N98027R00022 is issued as a request for proposal (RFP) for SNOMED CT and Related Services: U.S. national membership in SNOMED International and related services for SNOMED CT, as described in Attachment 1, Statement of Work. This acquisition is not set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Provisions and clauses incorporated by reference are the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) deviation versions. The National Institutes of Health, on behalf of the National Library of Medicine, intends to award a contract on a sole-source basis to the International Health Terminology Standards Development Organisation (IHTSDO), trading as SNOMED International, London, United Kingdom, under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented at RFO FAR 6.103-1. IHTSDO owns SNOMED CT and holds the intellectual property rights needed to provide U.S. national membership and the related services. Period of performance: a 12-month base period beginning January 1, 2027, plus four 12-month option periods. Primary place of performance: London, United Kingdom. Each period has two line items, each with a quantity of one lot: a U.S. national membership fee (Statement of Work Task 1) and a Managed Service Fee (Statement of Work Tasks 2 through 5). Deliverables will be delivered to and accepted by NLM in Bethesda, Maryland, FOB destination. Questions must be submitted by email to Michael Beadle, Contract Specialist (michael.beadle@nih.gov), and Linda E. Smith, Contracting Officer (linda.smith2@nih.gov), by November 25, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. ET. Proposals must be submitted by email to both points of contact by Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. ET. Include "RFP 75N98027R00022" in the subject line.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Helena, MT
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. Place of Performance The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT. Interested parties must be located no more than 50 miles from the Helena, MT area. Period of Performance On or about October 1, 2026 � September 30, 2030 (Base plus 3 option years) 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales pr

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Extension of Ordering Period for IDIQ Contract and Increase to IDIQ Ceiling for Contract 75N98020D00083, Cox Subscriptions, Inc.
description: Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source � Extension of Ordering Period for IDIQ Contract and Increase to IDIQ Ceiling for Contract 75N98020D00083, Cox Subscriptions, Inc. Reference Number: 75N98027Q00114 Description THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT MODIFICATION WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. The purpose of this announcement is for the Division of Library Services (DLS), within the Office of the Director (OD), National Institutes of Health, to issue a modification to the existing Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract number 75N98020D00083 on a sole source basis, under the authority of 41 U.S.C. �3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1: Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements and FAR 6.301-1(a)(2)(ii) to extend the ordering period of the existing IDIQ contract and increase the IDIQ ceiling with Cox Subscriptions, Inc., entitled �NIH Library Subscription Agent Services� The objective is to extend the ordering period and increase the IDIQ ceiling to ensure continued access to mission critical resources while the NIH procurement team continues to pursue the re-competition of these services under a new full and open IDIQ contract. This acquisition supports the continuation of mission-critical resources for NIH researchers and scientific staff. The Government would be harmed if this contract were allowed to expire on the current date of December 31, 2026, as thousands of medical journals, databases, and eBooks would no longer be available as reference material for ongoing scientific research. If access to these reference materials is interrupted or stopped before a new contract can be put into place, many years of funded effort and data will be in jeopardy. Therefore, it is essential that the current contractor, Cox Subscriptions, Inc., continue the work while the requirement is appropriately recompeted, as they provide capabilities and critical expertise necessary to meet NIH�s needs. The anticipated one-year extension to the contract�s ordering period is necessary to ensure continuity of mission-critical services and to allow sufficient time for the proper execution of a recompete. This approach ensures sufficient time for thorough review of proposals commensurate with the complexity of the requirement, while allowing a new contractor sufficient time to transition without interruption to operations. The ordering period end date will be extended by twelve (12) months to from December 31, 2026 to December 31, 2027. The IDIQ ceiling will be increased by $10,000,000.00 from $60,000,000.00 to $70,000,000.00. An extension of the ordering period and increase in the IDIQ ceiling is required to ensure continued access to mission critical resources while the NIH procurement team continues to pursue the re-competition of these services under a new full and open IDIQ contract. Cox Subscriptions, Inc., is the incumbent contractor and possesses unique experience essential to maintain continuity of operations. The contract requires uninterrupted access to thousands of scientific journals, scientific/medical databases, and eBooks. The loss of access to these mission critical resources would cause considerable loss to Government investment if support is not maintained by the current contractor until such time as a recompete can be completed. There will not be a solicitation of Request for Proposals (RFP) issued as a result of this announcement. Any responses or inquiries to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition will be advantageous to the Government. All information received from this notice shall be used for planning and market research purposes only. The statutory authority for this sole source action is implemented by FAR 6.302-1. Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy the agency�s requirements. The award is subject to approval of the Justification and Approval for Sole Source (J&A). Once the J&A is approved, this action will serve to change the IDIQ contract�s ordering period and IDIQ ceiling via a modification to the contract. Notwithstanding the stated intent, if other organizations believe they can fully meet the Government�s requirement, they must submit a written capabilities statement. The capabilities statement must contain sufficient documentation to establish a bona fide capability to fulfill the requirement and must be received by the response date listed in this posting. A determination not to compete with this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NIH will not be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the evaluation of the information received. Interested parties may respond and provide a capability statement no later than 12:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST), December 1, 2026, via email to Kevin Alvarez, Contracting Officer, at kevin.alvarez@nih.gov. Emails must reference the announcement number in the subject line. This is not an RFP, and this announcement does not commit the Government to award a contract. The reference number to be used is 75N98027Q00114.

Haley Veterans Hospital-Nursing Surgical Specialty Services, Tampa, FL. title: 5831--Vocera Service Agreement (VA-27-00015995)
description: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Chillicothe Medical Center Vocera Service and Support Request for Information (RFI) Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c)(2), Responses to RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who are able to meet Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for the Vocera Service and Support. Any contract/order that might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will be the outcome of the competitive process. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information to identify Authorized resellers for the Vocera Product to include Service and Support. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal (RFP), if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519 with a size standard of 150 Employees. Generic capability statements or marketing materials will not be accepted or reviewed. RFI Response Instructions NOTE: The capability package must be clear, concise, and complete. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI. Provide Company Information: Company Name Unique Entity Identifier Number (UEI) under which the company is registered in SAM Company Address Point of contact name Telephone number Email address Small Business size status based upon the applicable NAICS code of 541519. For more information refer to http://www.sba.gov/. If SDVOSB/VOSB, is your business verified in the VetCert database (https://veterans.certify.sba.gov) For small business concerns, indicate whether at least 50 percent of the total amount paid by the Government will be paid to firms that are similarly situated. List any existing contracting vehicles you currently maintain that cover the intended scope of work Brief summary describing your company s technical approach to meeting the requirements, to include; Company Background and Experience Can you provide an overview of your company and its experience in developing workforce analysis, specifically for government or healthcare organizations? What are some of your previous projects related to Workforce Assessments? What modernization initiatives would the solution offer? What best practices or implementation lessons learned can you share from deploying assessment programs in other large federal environments? Industry feedback Are there any requirements within the Product Description (PD) that are unclear, ambiguous, or require additional detail? If so, please identify the section(s) and provide recommended clarifications. Does the PD accurately reflect industry standards and best practices for the requested services? Please identify any areas where revisions may be beneficial. Are the performance objectives, deliverables, and acceptance criteria clearly defined and reasonable? If not, please provide suggested revisions. Are there any tasks, assumptions, or dependencies that should be added, removed, or modified to improve the overall effectiveness of the requirement? Does the proposed period of performance and level of effort appear realistic and achievable? Please provide rationale for any recommended changes. Are there any risks, challenges, or potential gaps in the PD that the Government should consider prior to issuing a solicitation? Please provide any additional comments, recommendations, or suggested revisions that would improve the clarity, accuracy, or feasibility of the PD. Responses to this RFI shall be submitted electronically by 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time, December 1, 2026 via email the Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) point of contacts: Contract Specialist, Harold Nice, Harold.Nice@va.gov and Contracting Officer Kimberly Geran, Kimberly.Geran@va.gov. Please note Response to RFI Vocera Service in the subject line of your response. Q&A cut-off date: November 27, 2026 by 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time WARNING: Please do not wait until the last minute to submit your responses! Please be advised that timeliness is determined by the date and time an Offeror s response is received by the Government not when an Offeror attempted transmission. Offerors are encouraged to review and ensure that sufficient bandwidth is available on their end of the transmission. All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the following: All proprietary/company confidential material shall be clearly marked on every page that contains such. No more than 5 pages (excluding cover sheet, table of contence page). Responses should be submitted in Microsoft Word format with Times New Roman font, 12 pt. minimum that addresses the above information. Interested parties should limit marketing material in order to allow sufficient space for adequately, directly, and substantively responding with the information of most interest to the Government. See attached: Draft PD Vocera Software Service Agreement VA will not be able to grant any extensions to this RFI.

title: USAFA TR Commercial Lodging Services
description: See Attachments Solicitation FA700027Q0010 has been amended on 19 Nov 2026 Amendment 1 Description The purpose of this amendment is to clarify Government requirements, add FAR 52.219-14 to Attachment 4 � Provisions and Clauses, and update the evaluation criteria. All previously uploaded attachments have been deleted and replaced with updated versions. Offerors MUST use the updated attachments when submitting their quotations. The following major changes have been incorporated into the solicitation package: 1. Updates to the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation: Third-Party Offerors (Brokers): Language has been added to Factor 1 clarifying that third-party management companies are permitted to quote, but they must explicitly identify the physical hotel property, provide a signed Letter of Commitment from that facility if it is not registered as a small business in the System for Award Management at sam.gov, and prove compliance with the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Capability Statement Additions: Offerors must now identify their dedicated Point of Contact (POC) for reservations, describe their reservation process, and affirmatively acknowledge the capability to meet a 24-hour response time. 2. Updates to the Requirement Statement (Attachment 1): Reservations & POC: Added Section 5.1, requiring a dedicated POC who must respond to authorized caller reservation requests within 24 hours. 3. Updates to Provisions and Clauses (Attachment 4): Limitations on Subcontracting: Added FAR 52.219-14 to enforce the 50% pass-through limit for small business set-asides. Offerors are advised to carefully review all updated attachments in their entirety prior to submitting a quote. Amendment 2 Description The purpose of this amendment is to provide further clarification based on industry questions and to correct minor administrative anomalies from the previous amendment. All previously uploaded attachments have been replaced with "_A2" versions. Offerors MUST use the "_A2" attachments when submitting their quotations. The following specific changes have been incorporated into the solicitation package: 1. Updates to the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (FA700027Q0010_A2): Factor 2 � Pricing (Annual Rate Updates): Restored language in the evaluation criteria clarifying that while rates for the Base Period (FY27) are fixed, BPA rates will be reviewed and updated bilaterally on an annual basis to coincide with the newly published GSA Fiscal Year lodging per diem rates. 2. Updates to the Requirement Statement (Attachment 1_A2): Mandatory Fitness Center: Reaffirmed in Sections 2.3 and 3.4 that a 24-hour fitness center (available 7 days a week) is a mandatory facility requirement for technical acceptability, and not a preferred amenity. 3. Clarification on Price Sheet (Attachment 2): The Price Sheet correctly reflects the Base Period as the remainder of Fiscal Year 2027 (January 2027 through September 2027). Offerors should only provide fixed nightly rates for these months. Important Dates: Questions Cut-Off Date: 24 November 2026 at 10:00 AM MST. Quote Due Date: 1 December 2026 at 10:00 AM MST. Offerors are advised to carefully review all updated "_A2" attachments in their entirety prior to submitting a quote. Update Description: Official Questions & Answers (Q&A) Posted The purpose of this update is to post the official Government responses to all industry questions received regarding Solicitation FA700027Q0010 (USAFA Transient Training Lodging BPA). Please see the newly attached document titled "Consolidated_QandA_FA700027Q0010" for the complete list of questions and answers. This document provides critical clarifications regarding evaluation criteria, third-party broker requirements, GSA per diem caps, and operational expectations. Please note that the deadline for submitting questions has now passed (24 November 2026 at 10:00 AM MST). The Government will not be accepting any further questions regarding this solicitation. Offerors are highly encouraged to thoroughly review the consolidated Q&A document, along with all previously posted "_A2" attachments, prior to submitting their quotations to ensure full compliance. Reminder: Quotations remain due no later than 1 December 2026 at 10:00 AM MST.

Capable of resolving 1.0mm Wire. Battery life of 8 hours. Withstand extreme temperatures. title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Helena, MT
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. Place of Performance The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT. Interested parties must be located no more than 50 miles from the Helena, MT area. Period of Performance On or about October 1, 2026 � September 30, 2026 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT, NOT A SOLICITATION FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. A SOLICITATION DOCUMENT WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND PROPOSALS WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. OALM intends to negotiate under RFO - FAR 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other suppliers or services will satisfy agency requirements. Authority: 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), with COX Subscription, Inc, to increase the contract ceiling to support the current ongoing activities extended from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027. The National Institutes of Health Division of Library Services (DLS) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of placing or renewing journal subscriptions in online and/or print formats and paying publisher invoices for subscriptions DLS has placed directly with publishers to be ready to start with no delay on January 1, 2027. This notice serves as a combined Sources Sought and Pre-Solicitation Notice to determine whether other responsible sources are available and capable of meeting the Government's requirements within the urgent timeframe along with notify the government�s intent to move forward on a sole source basis. OALM intends to negotiate, under authority of FAR 6.302-1 and HHSAR 306.302-1, on a sole source basis, with COX Subscriptions, inc. to increase the contract ceiling to support the current ongoing activities from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027. No other source is able to provide these critical/essential services beginning on January 1, 2027 without causing unacceptable delays to the Government in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. This sole source action is under the authority 41 U.S.C. 253(c)(1) as set forth in FAR 6.302-1 as it is impracticable to seek competition for the 44-day period while completing the acquisition process for the competitive requirement. The statutory authority also provides that other than full and open competition is appropriate for follow-on contracts when it is likely that the award of a contract to another source would result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government that would not be expected to be recovered through competition or that unacceptable delays would result. Delays would put those needing the services at risk. The current incumbent Contractor, Cox Subscription Inc, can provide seamless support for this requirement for the limited period of January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027 which is the time needed to complete the competitive acquisition process to award the follow-on contract. The National Institutes of Health Division of Library Services supports the information needs, including access to journal literature, of all researchers, clinical staff and administrators employed by NIH. Since 2004, DLS also has provided these services to a number of other agencies of the Health & Human Services Department (HHS). Over the last 20 years, the DLS has successfully shifted completely from print to online only access for the journal literature. Currently, nearly 14,000 journals are available from NIH desktops and through the HHS Digital Library. NIH or select groups within HHS may choose to acquire small, on-site print journal collections which DLS orders on their behalf. DLS requires qualified subscription agent with the experience and human, technical, and financial resources necessary to support its acquisition of online and, to a more limited extent, print journal subscriptions. The offeror must have the appropriate combination of the following intellectual and technical capabilities: Subscription Management System This web-based system should contain metadata records for all biomedical journals and databases common to a large biomedical research organization. The web-based system should be available to customers 24/7 with at least a 99% average reliability. A user-friendly dashboard with multiple account levels (and unlimited local accounts) should be available to support subscription management and collection development needs. This system must have complete metadata on all journals considered for acquisition (if a title is not in the agent�s database, it must be added within 2 days). Ability for customer to generate sortable, machine readable reports (Excel spreadsheets) using any of the above fields in any combination as needed. Ability to generate sortable reports of titles contained within subscription packages, including all of the information listed in 1e above. Ability to capture, store and display all bibliographic and financial transactions in the customer�s account for the previous five years. Ability to export and/or synchronize this information (all fields on all titles within all orders) using standard protocols into a commercial or open source electronic resources management system. Ability to clearly distinguish payment for a subscription placed by the offeror and one placed directly by the customer but paid by agent. Ability to interface with the customer�s integrated library system using standard EDI transfer, or a future standard that may be developed and adopted. Ability to support transmission of purchase orders and invoices electronically. Provide web-based access to all customer and payment related data, including proof of payment. Provide ability for customer to generate claims online Provide ability for customer to export reports in Excel format Provide address fields with maximum flexibility, with at least 5 lines and 30 characters\ per line. Subscription Services Ability to accept and pay any information provider invoices within two weeks of receipt on behalf of customer, whether or not the resource is subscribed to through the agent; and invoice customer within one week of payment to publisher. Traditional subscription agent services including working with publishers to obtain current prices for a list of publications, obtaining proper invoices and paying those invoices after customer approval. Ability to verify payment of invoices with information provider/publisher to the correct NIH account within 48 hours of subscription agent payment. Support for multiple subscription accounts within the web-based electronic resources and serials management system, including separate reporting, review and approvals for each account subscription list. Maintain records and provide reporting to show the amount spent, amount projected, and balance/deficit for each subscription account in the system. Variety of alerts and email reports to notify customer of changes to subscription mix including, but not limited to, changes in format, publisher, price increases above a pre-defined threshold, or discontinued titles. Ability to send customized messages to publishers meeting a specific selection criteria (identified by NIH Library) or to all publishers on an as needed basis. Maintain a current database of publisher point of contact information that can be used for alerting and renewal correspondence. title: East Bulkhead Replacement, East Boat Basin, Cape Cod Canal, Sandwich MA
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District will be issuing an Invitation for Bids for the East bulkhead Replacement project located in Sandwich, MA. This procurement is a Small Business Set Aside Invitation for Bid (IFB). The NAICS code for the work is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a size standard of $45M. Construction is expected to take about 23 months to complete, including a 12 month turf establishment period. The estimated construction cost is between $10,000,000.00 and $25,000,000.00. Any responsible contractor meeting this standard may submit a bid to be considered by the New England District. The East Boat Basin is a small sheltered harbor for small craft located near the east end of the Cape Cod Canal on the Cape side in Sandwich, Massachusetts. On both sides of the entrance to the harbor, facing the canal, are sheet pile bulkheads. This project will replace the east sheet pile bulkhead with a completely new bulkhead. Specific work tasks include, but are not limited to, the following: install approximately 950 linear feet of steel sheet piles with interior whalers to create a new bulkhead about five feet in front of the existing bulkhead sheets; install a system of wood fender piles to protect against ships and boats; cut off the existing steel sheet piles about 10 feet below grade, backfill the space between old and new sheet piles with crushed stone; install new concrete dead men, tie rods and waler connected to new PZ40 sheet piles; replace light system and existing conduits and protect existing associated power supply system; install new bollards, and cleats. This is not an invitation for bids at this time. The solicitation requirements and contract documents including instructions for submission and the response date will be available on or about December 1, 2026. Neither telephonic, mailed, nor faxed requests for hard copies of this solicitation will be accepted. The solicitation will only be available online; in order to download the solicitation, offerors must access the System of Award Management website (https://sam.gov/). All responsible sources may submit a bid which shall be considered by the New England District. Additional questions may be emailed to Kyle Hall, New England District Contract Specialist, at kyle.k.hall@usace.army.mil or by phone at (978) 318-8479
