title: MAZAK EQUIPMENT
description: NASA/Stennis Space Center has a requirement for 3 Mazak machines: o Mazak VTC-Ez 30 o Mazak 350 MY lathe with live tooling o Mazak 5-Axis Mill NASA/Stennis Space Center intends to award a sole-source firm-fixed-price contract for the acquisition of one MAZAK VTC-Ez 30 Vertical Machining Center, one MAZAK QUICK TURN 350MY Turning Center with Live Tooling, and one MAZAK VARIAXIS 5-Axis Machining Center. The proposed acquisition is being pursued pursuant to FAR 6.103-1(a)(1), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The Government has determined that only MAZAK brand equipment will satisfy its minimum requirements for machine shop standardization, compatibility with the existing MAZAK fleet, common CNC programming, operator proficiency, tooling, fixtures, maintenance procedures, and spare parts inventory. Acquisition of an alternative manufacturer's equipment would require substantial duplication of cost to the Government through retraining personnel, reprogramming existing manufacturing processes, establishing separate maintenance and spare parts inventories, and qualifying new production methods. These additional costs are not expected to be recovered through competition and would adversely impact operational efficiency and continuity. As a result, the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with Mazak Corporation and/or its authorized distributors as the only sources capable of providing the required MAZAK equipment. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Megan Calcote Megan.a.calcote@nasa.gov not later than 12:00 PM on December 1st, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

title: DRAFT RFP-03C27R00003-Large-Scale Fixed Systems (Multi-Energy Portal and Low-Energy Portal) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity Contact
description: Updated: Friday, November 27, 2026 MEP-LEP Industry Day Date: December 1, 2026 Time: 1:00pm EST. Virtual Event: Teams meeting invite after RSVP Purpose: The purpose of the industry day is to share additional information regarding the planned solicitation approach for MEP and LEP systems. It will afford vendors an opportunity to gain information on the IDIQ on-ramp and off-ramp process. Vendors may also ask questions during a dedicated Q&A session. Agenda: Introduction Estimated RFP Release Minimum Buy On-ramp and Off-ramp Summary response to Draft RFP Questions Open Q&A Session RSVP: In order to attend the Industry Day you must email your list of up to 4 attendees by Monday, Nov 30th at 4:00pm EST to ronetta.m.sweeney@cbp.dhs.gov and aga.frys@cbp.dhs.gov. Attendees will then receive a Teams Calendar invite. Updated: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 : This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice Only-Do Not Submit Offers* Accepting Questions until Monday, November 23, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST* DRAFT -RFP -Large-Scale Fixed Systems (Multi-Energy Portal and Low-Energy Portal) Multiple-Award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity Contact Note: Attachment 1- Draft SOW includes embedded attachments 01a- 10. Related Notice ID: Pre-Solicitation Notice :DHS-CBP-BECD-20162084 published on October 21, 2026 1.Points of contact: Aga Frys (Contracting Officer) and Ronetta Sweeney ( Contract Specialist) DHS-Customs & Border Protection Border Enforcement Contracting Division 1300 Pennsylvania Ave, NW Washington, DC 20229 2. The proposed contract action will be solicited using Full and Open Competition in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 6.101, and not be a small business set-aside under RFO Part 19 nor a local area set-aside under RFO Part 26. 3. NAICS Code: 334517 and PSC: 6665 4. Description: (i) The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Innovation and Strategy Directorate (ISD), Non-Intrusive Inspection Division (NIID), on behalf of the Office of Field Operations (OFO), has an immediate requirement for two types of Large-Scale Fixed System, the Low-Energy Portal (LEP) system and Multi-Energy Portal (MEP) system. The requirement for these Large-Scale Fixed Systems includes equipment, delivery, installation and civil works, image formatting for ingestion in CBP systems, testing, verification, documentation, interconnectivity within all systems, lifecycle support, warranties, and ancillary logistical services. The objective of this requirement is to establish two (2) multiple-award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts, with a five (5) year ordering period, to acquire Large-Scale Fixed Systems, MEP and LEP systems, to replace existing systems of advanced age with the modern technology capable of producing higher quality images, faster throughput, improved detection of potential threats and reduced inspection times of crossings along the Northern and Southwest Border. *Places of Performance: Various locations throughout the U.S. and U.S. Territories* (ii) CBP plans to use both RFO 12.201-2, Other Procedures, in conjunction with RFO Part 15 ,Contracting by Negotiation, procedures to award these multiple-award IDIQ contracts in Quarter two (2) of fiscal year (FY) 2027. (iii) One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. (iv) No responses are required at this time; however, questions may be considered by interested parties. Interested parties my submit their questions to aga.frys@cbp.dhs.gov and ronetta.m.sweeney@cbp.dhs.gov no later than Monday, November 23, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. All responsible sources may submit a proposal for both MEP and LEP Systems or either MEP or LEP System in response to the issuance of the formal request for proposal (RFP) which will be considered by the agency. CBP anticipates releasing the formal RFP in Quarter one (1) of FY 2027.

description: AMENDMENT 001 was posted on 04 November 2026. Amendment 001 was established to extend the proposal submission due date to 01 December 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division, Lakehurst, New Jersey, intends to issue a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract on a competitive basis for the procurement of the Tail Rotor Balance Indicator, PN: 18D12545-1. This item is in support of the FMS Bahrain and Czech Republic H-1 Programs. The solicitation is being issued as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside in accordance with FAR Part 19. In accordance with the attachments in this solicitation, the submitted proposals must be accompanied by all supporting data and facts used to develop the proposal that are accurate, current, and complete, to allow Government evaluators to make their independent assessments. A proposal received without suffecient supporting data and rationale, such as inadequate cost/pricing data, will delay the procurement award and/or will result the proposal being rejected by the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO). In the event that the Contractor or any of its subcontractors have non-complying existing deficiencies, the Government requests that these deficiencies be reported to the PCO as soon as they are known. All requests for the TDP shall be requested from the Government via email at Christopher.d.brake5.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 1:00 PM EST on 19 November 2026, and shall be accompanied by a valid and current DD2345. ***This solicitation includes DFARS 252.204-7025, Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Requirements. The Technical Data Package (TDP) contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Offerors must obtain access to the CUI Drawing Package to prepare a proposal. Proof of CMMC Level 2 (Self-Assessment) certification is required to request access to the Technical Data Package. ***Proposals submitted should be in accordance with the attached document titled, "CLIN STRUCTURE". Proposals submitted to the Government not in accordance with the attachment, "CLIN STRUCTURE" will not be subject for Government evaluation/consideration of this requirement. ***Proposals shall be submitted no later than 01 December 2026 at 1:00 PM EST to Christopher Brake.

title: Air Force Civil Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Design Build Construction for Selective Improvement Project in Hong Kong Consulate � Sources Sought/Market Research
description: Department of State 2027 Design-Build Construction for Hong Kong Existing Consulate Compound (ECC) Selective Improvements Project (SIP) Sources Sought Market Research This is a Sources Sought Notice Only. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of U.S. Department of State market research and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP). The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified businesses, with a special interest in Small Business (SB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a), and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms under NAICS code 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Be advised that acquisition strategy and set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government is requesting information regarding the availability of capable firms to support the requirements of the U.S. Department of State (DOS), Bureau of Overseas Buildings Operations (OBO) for a Design-Build (DB) construction contract at the existing U.S. Consulate General compound in Hong Kong, S.A.R., China. Please note that a decision not to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future solicitation. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice, nor will it compensate responders for any costs incurred in the development or furnishing of a response. 1. Project Description � Hong Kong Existing Consulate Compound (ECC) Selective Improvements Project (SIP), Design-Build Construction TOP SECRET FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCES ARE REQUIRED. A Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Top-Secret facility security clearance (FCL) with Secret safeguarding capability is required for this project, along with an OBO/SPC approved dedicated project space, OBO/DT-approved classified Information System (IS) and ProjNet-C for handling classified information up to the Secret level. Property Description: The project is located at the existing U.S. Consulate General compound, 26 Garden Rd, Central, Hong Kong. The site comprises 1.42 acres in the Central Business District of Hong Kong and is bounded along its perimeter by Garden Rd, Lower Albert Rd, and Upper Albert Rd. The site is fully developed and occupied. Background: The Design-Build solicitation will follow a bridging design effort (Task Order awarded to an A/E IDIQ contractor) that is developing concept, Design Intent 1 (DI-1), and Design Intent 2 (DI-2) design packages to support an eventual Design-Build Request for Proposal. Project Scope: The project will address deficiencies in life safety, infrastructure, and space utilization at the existing, occupied consulate compound. Key scope elements may include: Provide code-compliant emergency egress and fire sprinkler piping Replace/add chillers and other mechanical infrastructure (air-handling units, Building Automation System) Upgrade electrical and telecommunications infrastructure Provide accessible pathways for all consular functions Improve space utilization Replace roof and repair minor structural deficiencies Important and Unique Considerations: This project requires phasing and logistics to maintain existing post operations with minimal disruption, as the compound must remain fully functional throughout construction. The Design-Build offeror will be expected to develop a constructability analysis, phasing plan, and project execution schedule showing how work will be accomplished with limited swing space and very limited on-site storage/laydown area in an occupied, secure diplomatic facility. Estimated Construction Cost & Contract Type: The design-build project is currently estimated to be between $65,000,000 - $95,000,000, representing the estimated construction cost at award, inclusive of all direct and indirect costs to be incurred by the General Contractor for full delivery of the project scope. The contract type for this project is Firm-Fixed Price. Estimated Design-Build Contract Period: The related Bridging Design task order period runs September 2026 through July 2027. The anticipated design/build construction duration is approximately four years, with award planned for early FY2028. 2. Capability Statement Requirements Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11-inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide all the following requested information: a) Company information � Company name, System for Award Management Unique Entity Identification number (SAM UEI), address, point of contact name, phone number, and email address. b) Company's business size and socioeconomic status for the applicable NAICS code 236220, such as: Certified HUBZone, Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), 8(a) Participant, Small Business, or Other than Small Business (Large Business). c) Experience and capability � Provide experience and demonstrate capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past eight (8) years. Each example should include: i. A brief description of the project ii. Description of the work performed, including identification of self-performance and/or subcontractor management iii. Customer name iv. Timeliness of performance v. Dollar value of the project vi. Any challenges experienced during the project, including delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management or organizational issues, or other significant challenges Given the classified/secure and occupied-facility nature of this project, firms should also highlight experience with: Design-Build construction in occupied, secure U.S. diplomatic or comparably classified facilities Personnel holding or able to obtain DCSA Top Secret facility and personnel security clearances Overseas construction logistics, phasing, and limited-laydown-area execution d) Bonding capability � Provide bonding capability in the form of a surety letter. Please submit all capability statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page maximum above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Responses will not restrict the Government to any particular acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. 3. Closing Deadline for Submissions ALL ELECTRONIC SUBMISSIONS MUST BE RECEIVED BY 2:00 P.M. Eastern Time on December 01, 2026. Please provide submission responses and/or questions via email to Lenny Le at LELT@state.gov and Patrick Reilly at reillypa2@state.gov.

title: Military construction management services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT FOR INDEFINITE DELIVERY CONTRACT (IDC) SINGLE AWARD TASK ORDER CONTRACT (SATOC) FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES PRIMARILY FOR Military construction to include SRM for THE U.S. ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS, NEW YORK DISTRICT (NAN), CONTINENTAL UNITED STATES (CONUS) . PURPOSE: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. This announcement is issued solely for information and planning purposes as part of the Government's market research and acquisition planning efforts. The purpose of this notice is to obtain feedback from industry regarding the requirements detailed under the "Description of the Requirement" section below. Industry input will assist the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in identifying capable and available sources to meet these requirements and may influence the development of the official solicitation packages. Futhermore, this announcement is to also gain knowledge of potential business sources; with specific interest in small business, certified 8(a) serviced by SBA districts, certified HUB Zone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). This notice does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service, and the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541618 (Other Management Consulting Services), with a corresponding Small Business Size Standard of [$19.0 Million]. If respondents believe a more appropriate NAICS code applies to the detailed requirement, please include this feedback and justification in your response. INTRODUCTION: The USACE, NAN, is conducting market research to identify capable and interested contractors to provide Construction Management Services within the CONUS Area of Responsibility (AOR). As permitted by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201(e), this is a market research tool being utilized for informational and planning purposes. Responses will assist the Government in developing its acquisition strategy for one or more potential Requests for Proposal to be issued at a later date. The determination of the final acquisition strategy lies solely with the Government and will be based on the results of this market research, along with information available from other sources. Specifically, this market survey is being conducted to determine if there is an adequate number of qualified firms capable of performing the required work in the specified locations. If your firm is interested, possesses a record of successful past performance on similar requirements, and has the capacity to fulfill the scope of work outlined below, you are highly encouraged to submit a response. Firms of all business sizes operating under the applicable NAICS code are invited to participate. Please be advised that the Government will not consider respondent experience performing Architect-Engineer (A-E) services (as defined by the Brooks Act and FAR Part 2) or construction services (as defined by FAR Parts 2 and 36) for this requirement. NEITHER PROPOSALS NOR QUOTES WILL BE ACCEPTED OR CONSIDERED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. Participation in this market research is strictly voluntary. Submitting a response to this notice is not a prerequisite to participate in any future formal RFP process. However, industry is advised that the information gathered through this notice may significantly influence the Government�s final acquisition strategy. All interested parties will be required to respond separately to any official solicitations posted at a later date. DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Place of Performance: Work will be performed predominantly within the USACE, New York District CONUS AOR. However, services may also be required anywhere within the broader USACE North Atlantic Division (NAD) CONUS AOR. Period of Performance: The anticipated duration for the Single Award Task Order Contract(s) is a five (5) year base ordering period. The contract(s) will expire at the end of the five (5) year period or when the maximum contract capacity is reached, whichever occurs first. Acquisition Information: The Government is currently contemplating the award of two (2) SATOCs. The maximum capacity for each SATOC is anticipated to be approximately $30 million. The services required under the anticipated SATOCs are non-personal services and do not include any inherently governmental functions. Activities/Services: The following items constitute a list of activities/services that are typically associated with construction management services (CMS): Cost estimates for contract changes. Reviews to confirm compliance with the solicitation and accepted (construction) proposal. Review contract claims. Preparation of cost estimates for change orders. Review and/or prepare construction phase reports and plans. Building Information Modeling (BIM) reviews of contractor drawing updates. Review of catalog cutsheets. Shop drawings that are not extensions of designs. Shop drawings that do not contain variations from the specified design. Review of material samples for noncritical materials. Administrative support. Photography/videos for progress reports. Construction materials control testing and reporting. Material quantity verification. Estimating quantities of project changes or change orders. Review contractor payrolls and perform labor standards interviews in the field. Prepare observations for Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS). Monitor contractor�s accident prevention plan. Conduct a mutual understanding meeting with the contractor on safety. Review contractor�s quality control (QC) plan prior to allowing work to begin. Conduct a coordination meeting with the contractor on QC prior to allowing work to begin. Submittal reviews that are for information only (FIO). Submittal and shop drawing reviews (not considered to be an extension of design, those for which government approval is not required). Monitor submittal register (timely submittals, approval of equipment/material, complete list). Review contractor schedule for accuracy with submittal register (review project schedule updates). Verify all warranties have been received. Review/verify QC test result reports. Review contractor daily QC reports. Quality assurance (QA) participation in three-phase inspections. QA minimum 5% verification testing (concrete, soils, etc.). QA observation of 10% of contractor QC tests. Monitor contractor deficiency log to confirm acceptable corrective actions. Perform field observations to confirm that contractor payments do not include nonconforming work. Prepare QA reports for each day the job is visited. Off-site inspection of fabricated items. Pre-final completion inspections for government acceptance (not final inspection for acceptance). Review of contractor insurance certificates and bonding. Contractor schedule review and monitoring. Weekly coordination meetings on non-design-related issues (quality, safety, schedule, contract admin). CMS (import/export, Quality Control System (QCS) training, etc.). Request for information (RFI) response to contractor requests for routine clarifications on contract requirements (not design clarifications). Review of operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals. Warranty response and enforcement. Attend partnering meetings with contractors. Evaluate/review unusually severe weather delays (monthly). Review and prepare accident reports. Document and report high-hazard activities (near miss reporting). Document small business (SB) subcontracting plan compliance monitoring. Contractor Personnel Identity Verification Presidential Directive (Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12). Attend post-award conference/preconstruction conference. title: National Coast Guard Museum- Facility Maintenance Services
description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, including small businesses (such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB), to provide comprehensive 24/7 Facility Maintenance services for the newly constructed National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut. The selected contractor will be required to furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant museum operations. The facility consists of an 84,000 sq. ft., six-story waterfront building situated on under 1 acre of grounds. Core requirements include, but are not limited to: HVAC & Environmental Controls: Continuous operation and maintenance of gas-fired condensing boilers, chillers, cooling towers, radiant flooring, and Building Automation Systems (BAS) to maintain strict gallery climate tolerances (68�F�72�F and 45%�55% Relative Humidity). Electrical, Plumbing, & Life Safety: Operations and maintenance of power distribution panels, emergency generators, fuel systems, fire alarms, fire extinguishers (NFPA 10), and water sprinkler systems (NFPA 25). Vertical Transportation: Monthly servicing, emergency response, and annual certified load testing for four (4) elevators. Custodial Services: A hybrid staffing model providing APPA Level 1 (Orderly Spotlessness) cleaning standards in high-traffic public galleries and APPA Level 4 in back-of-house staff areas. Grounds, Hardscape, & Snow Removal: Year-round exterior upkeep, power washing, and 24/7 bare-pavement snow and ice control (utilizing hardscape-safe compounds) for walkways, terraces, and flat roofing. Support Services: Integrated Pest Management (artifact-safe), catering kitchen equipment upkeep, and refuse/recycling stream management. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. This announcement is issued solely for information and planning purposes as part of the Government's market research and acquisition planning efforts. The purpose of this notice is to obtain feedback from industry regarding the requirements detailed under the "Description of the Requirement" section below. Industry input will assist the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in identifying capable and available sources to meet these requirements and may influence the development of the official solicitation packages. Futhermore, this announcement is to also gain knowledge of potential business sources; with specific interest in small business, certified 8(a) serviced by SBA districts, certified HUB Zone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). This notice does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service, and the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541618 (Other Management Consulting Services), with a corresponding Small Business Size Standard of $19.0 Million. If respondents believe a more appropriate NAICS code applies to the detailed requirement, please include this feedback and justification in your response. INTRODUCTION: The USACE, NAN, is conducting market research to identify capable and interested contractors to provide Construction Management Services within the CONUS Area of Responsibility (AOR). As permitted by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201(e), this is a market research tool being utilized for informational and planning purposes. Responses will assist the Government in developing its acquisition strategy for one or more potential Requests for Proposal to be issued at a later date. The determination of the final acquisition strategy lies solely with the Government and will be based on the results of this market research, along with information available from other sources. Specifically, this market survey is being conducted to determine if there is an adequate number of qualified firms capable of performing the required work in the specified locations. If your firm is interested, possesses a record of successful past performance on similar requirements, and has the capacity to fulfill the scope of work outlined below, you are highly encouraged to submit a response. Firms of all business sizes operating under the applicable NAICS code are invited to participate. Please be advised that the Government will not consider respondent experience performing Architect-Engineer (A-E) services (as defined by the Brooks Act and FAR Part 2) or construction services (as defined by FAR Parts 2 and 36) for this requirement. NEITHER PROPOSALS NOR QUOTES WILL BE ACCEPTED OR CONSIDERED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. Participation in this market research is strictly voluntary. Submitting a response to this notice is not a prerequisite to participate in any future formal RFP process. However, industry is advised that the information gathered through this notice may significantly influence the Government�s final acquisition strategy. All interested parties will be required to respond separately to any official solicitations posted at a later date. DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Place of Performance: Work will be performed predominantly within the USACE, New York District CONUS AOR. However, services may also be required anywhere within the broader USACE North Atlantic Division (NAD) CONUS AOR. Period of Performance: The anticipated duration for the Single Award Task Order Contract(s) is a five (5) year base ordering period. The contract(s) will expire at the end of the five (5) year period or when the maximum contract capacity is reached, whichever occurs first. Acquisition Information: The Government is currently contemplating the award of two (2) SATOCs. The maximum capacity for each SATOC is anticipated to be approximately $30 million. The services required under the anticipated SATOCs are non-personal services and do not include any inherently governmental functions. Activities/Services: The following items constitute a list of activities/services that are typically associated with construction management services (CMS): Cost estimates for contract changes. Reviews to confirm compliance with the solicitation and accepted (construction) proposal. Review contract claims. Preparation of cost estimates for change orders. Review and/or prepare construction phase reports and plans. Building Information Modeling (BIM) reviews of contractor drawing updates. Review of catalog cutsheets. Shop drawings that are not extensions of designs. Shop drawings that do not contain variations from the specified design. Review of material samples for noncritical materials. Administrative support. Photography/videos for progress reports. Construction materials control testing and reporting. Material quantity verification. Estimating quantities of project changes or change orders. Review contractor payrolls and perform labor standards interviews in the field. Prepare observations for Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS). Monitor contractor�s accident prevention plan. Conduct a mutual understanding meeting with the contractor on safety. Review contractor�s quality control (QC) plan prior to allowing work to begin. Conduct a coordination meeting with the contractor on QC prior to allowing work to begin. Submittal reviews that are for information only (FIO). Submittal and shop drawing reviews (not considered to be an extension of design, those for which government approval is not required). Monitor submittal register (timely submittals, approval of equipment/material, complete list). Review contractor schedule for accuracy with submittal register (review project schedule updates). Verify all warranties have been received. Review/verify QC test result reports. Review contractor daily QC reports. Quality assurance (QA) participation in three-phase inspections. QA minimum 5% verification testing (concrete, soils, etc.). QA observation of 10% of contractor QC tests. Monitor contractor deficiency log to confirm acceptable corrective actions. Perform field observations to confirm that contractor payments do not include nonconforming work. Prepare QA reports for each day the job is visited. Off-site inspection of fabricated items. Pre-final completion inspections for government acceptance (not final inspection for acceptance). Review of contractor insurance certificates and bonding. Contractor schedule review and monitoring. Weekly coordination meetings on non-design-related issues (quality, safety, schedule, contract admin). CMS (import/export, Quality Control System (QCS) training, etc.). Request for information (RFI) response to contractor requests for routine clarifications on contract requirements (not design clarifications). Review of operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals. Warranty response and enforcement. Attend partnering meetings with contractors. Evaluate/review unusually severe weather delays (monthly). Review and prepare accident reports. Document and report high-hazard activities (near miss reporting). Document small business (SB) subcontracting plan compliance monitoring. Contractor Personnel Identity Verification Presidential Directive (Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12). Attend post-award conference/preconstruction conference. Preparation of QA plans and execution of QA plans. Train contractors in QCS system. Review safety plan. Construction-rela

description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, including small businesses (such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB), to provide comprehensive 24/7 Facility Maintenance services for the newly constructed National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut. The facility consists of an 84,000 sq. ft., six-story waterfront building situated on under 1 acre of grounds. Core requirements include, but are not limited to: HVAC & Environmental Controls: Continuous operation and maintenance of gas-fired condensing boilers, chillers, cooling towers, radiant flooring, and Building Automation Systems (BAS) to maintain strict gallery climate tolerances (68�F�72�F and 45%�55% Relative Humidity). Vertical Transportation: Monthly servicing, emergency response, and annual certified load testing for four (4) elevators. Custodial Services: A hybrid staffing model providing APPA Level 1 (Orderly Spotlessness) cleaning standards in high-traffic public galleries and APPA Level 4 in back-of-house staff areas. Grounds, Hardscape, & Snow Removal: Year-round exterior upkeep, power washing, and 24/7 bare-pavement snow and ice control (utilizing hardscape-safe compounds) for walkways, terraces, and flat roofing. Support Services: Integrated Pest Management (artifact-safe), catering kitchen equipment upkeep, and refuse/recycling stream management. description: Anticipated Period of Performance The anticipated period of performance is February 1, 2027 through January 31, 2028, with an option to extend services for an additional 6 month period, through July 31, 2028. Anticipated award date: February 1, 2027 The NAICS Code is 541715. Introduction The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) supports research related to the basic understanding of microbiology and immunology leading to the development of vaccines, therapeutics, and medical diagnostics for the prevention, treatment, and diagnosis of infectious and immune-mediated diseases. The NIAID, Division of Allergy, Immunology, and Transplantation (DAIT) has a requirement to support a broad range of services critical for the design, development, execution, and analysis of clinical research in autoimmune diseases. The major clinical research programs to be supported by this solicitation include, Autoimmunity Centers of Excellence and Immune Tolerance Network (ACE), as well as investigator initiated clinical trials (IICT), and other clinical trials or study activities supported by NIAID herein collectively referred to as NIAID supported research. Description Topic Title: Autoimmune Diseases Statistical & Clinical Coordinating Center (ADSCCC) The Division of Allergy, Immunology, and Transplantation (DAIT), National Institutes of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), project is for work related to the contract below: �Autoimmune Diseases Statistical & Clinical Coordinating Center (AD-SCCC)�, RHO Federal Systems Division, Inc. (Contract 75N93022C00003) This contract was awarded on a competitive basis for a five-year period from February 1, 2022 through January 31, 2027. A term type/level of effort contract was awarded for the delivery of 56,170 direct labor hours per year for Years 1-5. The total value of the contract is $49,268,667 and includes options for extension of the term for a total performance period of 5 years and options for increases in the level of effort, with the purpose of establishing an Autoimmune Diseases Statistical & Clinical Coordinating Center (AD- SCCC) that will provide a broad range of support critical for the design, development, execution, and analysis of clinical research sponsored by NIAID in autoimmune diseases and diseases related to mucosal immunology and primary immune deficiencies. The scope of clinical research to be supported by the AD- SCCC includes: (i) clinical trials at all phases to evaluate the safety and efficacy of investigational products and innovative approaches for disease treatment and prevention; (ii) studies of underlying mechanisms as integral components of clinical trials; (iii) clinical studies (e.g., genetic studies, microbiome studies, surveys of current therapies, etc.); and (iv) surrogate/biomarker studies. The scope of statistical and clinical support functions to be performed by the AD-SCCC includes statistical design and analysis; protocol development; study initiation and management; clinical safety and pharmacovigilance support; safety oversight; management of clinical study collaboration portals; manuscript preparation and management of sample repositories. The NIAID, NIH, conducts and supports basic and applied research to better understand, treat, and ultimately prevent infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases. The causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of autoimmune diseases are major areas of emphasis for NIAID�s Division of Allergy, Immunology, and Transplantation (DAIT). DAIT pursues research on autoimmune diseases by supporting investigator-initiated research projects, cooperative clinical studies, national networks of research centers, and demonstration and education research projects. A critical component of the Division�s mission focuses on clinical research to develop new and/or improved strategies to treat or prevent autoimmune diseases through rigorous evaluations of the safety and efficacy of investigational products and therapeutic interventions, studies to elucidate underlying mechanisms of disease, studies to develop and evaluate surrogate/biomarkers of disease stage, severity and progression, and clinical studies of disease natural history. The purpose of this acquisition is to extend the period of performance of the current contract (through July 31, 2028), beginning February 1, 2027, thereby maintaining the same direct labor hours to maintain ongoing clinical trial operations while DAIT completes the competition under the Clinical Data, Safety, and Coordinating Centers (CDSCC) NOFO. The extension retains the existing scope and contract type. The required research and development clinical trial activities are severable in nature, the 18-month extension will be structured as two discrete option periods. Specifically, the Contractor will be responsible for the following: A. Statistical Design Provide expertise, advice and assistance pin the development of statistical design plans for the development of concept and full study proposals for NIAID supported clinical research; Provide assistance in the preparation of concept and full proposals and study-specific protocols; Provide assistance in the preparation of concept and full proposals and protocols for mechanistic studies; Provide support for preclinical safety study evaluation by providing statistical expertise for, and participate in, evaluating the accuracy and validity of data from preclinical safety studies in support of clinical trials if applicable; Provide assistance for clinical trials and mechanistic studies post-study initiation. B. Statistical Analysis Development and preparation of the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for each clinical trial in conjunction with the Study Management Teams (SMTs); Preparation of interim and final analyses; Preparation of summary data reports; Development and preparation of results for posting as required by ClinicalTrials.gov; Review of the accuracy and completeness of statistical data and data analyses for all abstracts, manuscripts, and presentations reporting on the clinical studies conducted by the relevant NIAID-sponsored networks and investigators prior to presentation or submission for publication. Collaboration with NIAID-supported research, including the NIAID Clinical Data and Safety Management Center (CDSMC); C. Protocol Development and Study Initiation Provide expert advice and assistance to SMTs in the development of protocols for clinical trials and mechanistic studies; Provide expert advice, assistance and coordination in the preparation, writing, review and approval of protocol-related documents and materials in collaboration with NIAID, SMTs, and the CDSMC and other NIAID supported research. D. Data Management and Reporting E. Clinical Safety and Pharmacovigilance Center Support F. Safety Oversight Structure Support G. Clinical Study Internet-Based Collaboration Portals H. Training I. Repository of Biological Specimens J. Other Technical and Administrative Support K. Scientific and Technical Personnel L. Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources M. Quality Assurance/Quality Control N. Overall Project Management O. Initial and Final Transitions The NIAID intends to negotiate, under the authority of RFO - FAR Part 6.302-1 and HHSAR Part 306.302-1, on a sole source basis with Rho, to modify the existing contract to extend the current contract by a total of 18-months [Term Option 5 (12-months, February 1, 2027 through January 31, 2028), and Term Option 6 (6-months, February 1, 2028 through July 31, 2028)]. title: Air Force Civil Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: C222--589-27-108, Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Building 26 KCVA (ME) FY27 NRM VISN Base - AE (VA-27-00021035)
description: DESCRIPTION Project: 589-27-108 Solicitation Number: 36C25527Q0057 RFP: 36C25527R0018 Title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Type of Notice: Sources Sought Posted Date:11/16/2026 Response Date: 12/1/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: C222 -Architect and Engineering- Electrical Systems NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for SF330's or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the VA Medical Center located in Kansas City, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 541330 Engineering Services and the size standard is $25.5 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail to matthew.finley@va.gov and received no later than December 1, 2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Business Opportunities website https://www.fbo.gov once available. Period of Performance for all design work is 150 calendar days including time for VA reviews. Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-75, the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73. The prime architect shall provide written certification of this to the Contracting Officer with the response provided for this market research. GENERAL SCOPE OF DESIGN: The Architect/Engineer (A/E)) shall provide professional design services for a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, uninterruptible power, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center (KCVA), 4801 Linwood Blvd, Kansas City, MO 64128. A/E Part One Services (also known as the design phase) for this design project encompass site visits as needed, field investigations, and the conduct of studies and user interviews to prepare detailed drawings, specifications, and cost estimates. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate and provide construction period services for a construction project. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center. The A/E services are required for preparation of Narrative, Studies, Phasing Design, Schematic Designs, Design Development, Construction Documents, and As Built Documents. The A/E shall coordinate all disciplines necessary to deliver a complete electrical infrastructure project. The A/E shall not rely solely on record drawings and shall verify existing conditions before using them as the basis of design. Ensuring all required permits and licenses from federal, state/provincial, or local authorities are obtained for the construction, installation, and operation of the equipment is also part of the A/E s responsibilities. The project design will comply with Infection Control and Interim Life Safety Measures. The A/E will provide design drawing, specification, and IGCE submissions at 35% (Schematic Design), 65% (Design Development), 95% (Construction Documents), and Final Bid Documents for all disciplines necessary to complete the project to the VA. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 541330 and qualified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned small business under NAICS code 541330. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 541330. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on December 21, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Project 589-27-108 Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26," IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://beta.sam.gov/. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ . title: Helmet-Mounted First-Person View Display System
description: I. Description USSOCOM is conducting market research to identify sources capable of providing dismounted Special Operations Forces with a helmet-mounted first-person view (FPV) display. This display must deliver an expanded field of view, certified ballistic protection, real-time tactical information overlay, and unmanned system control in contested, congested, and all-weather environments. The effort aims to develop a 50-degree field-of-view Display Module that integrates full military ballistic protection, ATAK capability, head tracking, improved display performance, and expanded environmental durability while remaining compatible with existing soldier systems and helmets. This announcement is for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation. The Government will use responses to this notice to assess interest and capability within the industry and to determine the acquisition strategy (e.g., limited competition or small business set-aside). This Sources Sought is posted as a Call to Vulcan and all responses must be submitted to Vulcan. II. Requested Information Interested vendors are requested to submit the following information: Company Information: Company name, address, point of contact, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CMMC/NIST (type, date, score), website. Business Size: Indicate your business size and socio-economic status (e.g., small business, 8(a), HUBZone, etc.). Confirm your business size relative to 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). Security Clearance: Indicate your current facility clearance and the level of facility security clearances you can maintain. Relevant Experience: Provide a brief overview of your experience in supporting SOF, system testing, commercial integration, and ATAK areas as listed below. If no experience, briefly identify the names and CAGE codes of any small businesses that have demonstrated experience that your company can team/partner with on this requirement. Display Systems. System testing (researching, planning, designing, developing, analyzing, and testing a variety of electronic equipment and systems, military command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C5ISR) systems, interface units, and other electronic devices and test equipment) to support enhanced situational awareness, command and control, and precision effects while retaining mobility, protection, and compatibility with existing soldier equipment. Experience with existing soldier equipment (ATAK EUD, radios, hubs). Experience with researching, testing, and integrating emerging technologies as they pertain to real-time overlay of ATAK tactical data, targeting information, and UAS video/control in day, night, and all-weather contested environments. Capability Statement: Submit a capability statement that responds to the following questions: Describe your company�s relevant experience providing SOF support in any of the following areas: ATAK interface, ballistic protection integration, development testing, head tracking sensor integration, software updates and integration, integrating processing hardware and the Display Module into a single module, Windblast compatibility, Expanded environmental envelope, similar requirements or related mission sets. Include contract numbers, customers, and scope. Explain your approach to development milestones (SRR, PDR, CDR, development tests, prototype deliveries) for the combined work scope versus individual items and identify any related any similar efforts. Confirm your company�s ability to maintain adherence to milestones and react to shifts within technology or supply chains to avoid impact to development and enable future scaling of production. Describe your recruiting, screening, and retention strategy for specialized Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Explain how your company would manage and execute a contract for this development. What program management tools, structures, or practices will ensure successful delivery? Describe your Quality Assurance/Quality Control processes and how they would ensure compliance with the Statement of Objectives (SOO), Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) and Key System Attributes (KSAs). If applicable, identify any suppliers, subcontractors or teaming partners. Specify their roles and the percentage of work they are expected to perform. Identify any services within the SOO that meet the definition of commercial services under FAR 2.101. Provide catalog pricing or related contract references. Provide feedback on a recommendation on contract type and structure (length, phases, single award, FFP/CPFF, OTA). Are there any risks or constraints that may affect your participation? Identify how the USSOCOM can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion. Recommendations to improve the approach/specifications/NAICS/PSC/ DRAFT SOO to acquiring the identified items/services. III. Submission Details Submission Deadline: 3:00 Eastern on 01-DEC-2026 Submission Location: All submissions shall be made within https://vulcan-sof.com/ Submit To: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=a26a99ef-c351-464f-af93-dbcc064df521 IV. Disclaimer This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not reimburse costs incurred in response preparation. Participation in this notice is not a guarantee of future contract award.

title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: Title: SIOP MMDD MACC. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) has a requirement to provide predominantly construction services (design build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB)) for heavy and civil engineering waterfront facilities as well as commercial and institutional facilities primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock (MMDD) at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of NAVFAC Pacific. This solicitation will result in the award of Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC). The period of performance will be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. Each MACC holder will receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. This solicitation is unrestricted allowing for full and open competition. Large businesses are advised that an acceptable small business subcontracting plan is required. Primary North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M.Secondary NAICS code 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M. title: C222--589-27-108, Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Building 26 KCVA (ME) FY27 NRM VISN Base - AE (VA-27-00021035)
description: DESCRIPTION Project: 589-27-108 Solicitation Number: 36C25527Q0057 RFP: 36C25527R0018 Title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Type of Notice: Sources Sought Posted Date:11/16/2026 Response Date: 12/1/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: C222 -Architect and Engineering- Electrical Systems NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for SF330's or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the VA Medical Center located in Kansas City, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 541330 Engineering Services and the size standard is $25.5 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail to matthew.finley@va.gov and received no later than December 1, 2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Business Opportunities website https://www.fbo.gov once available. Period of Performance for all design work is 150 calendar days including time for VA reviews. Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-75, the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73. The prime architect shall provide written certification of this to the Contracting Officer with the response provided for this market research. GENERAL SCOPE OF DESIGN: The Architect/Engineer (A/E)) shall provide professional design services for a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, uninterruptible power, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center (KCVA), 4801 Linwood Blvd, Kansas City, MO 64128. A/E Part One Services (also known as the design phase) for this design project encompass site visits as needed, field investigations, and the conduct of studies and user interviews to prepare detailed drawings, specifications, and cost estimates. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate and provide construction period services for a construction project. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center. The A/E services are required for preparation of Narrative, Studies, Phasing Design, Schematic Designs, Design Development, Construction Documents, and As Built Documents. The A/E shall coordinate all disciplines necessary to deliver a complete electrical infrastructure project. The A/E shall not rely solely on record drawings and shall verify existing conditions before using them as the basis of design. Ensuring all required permits and licenses from federal, state/provincial, or local authorities are obtained for the construction, installation, and operation of the equipment is also part of the A/E s responsibilities. The project design will comply with Infection Control and Interim Life Safety Measures. The A/E will provide design drawing, specification, and IGCE submissions at 35% (Schematic Design), 65% (Design Development), 95% (Construction Documents), and Final Bid Documents for all disciplines necessary to complete the project to the VA. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 541330 and qualified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned small business under NAICS code 541330. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 541330. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on December 21, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Project 589-27-108 Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26," IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://beta.sam.gov/. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs; Network 15 Contracting Office; 3450 S. 4th Street, Leavenworth, KS 66048 Point of Contact(s): Matt Finley, Contracting Officer, e-mail address: Matthew.Finley@va.gov

title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ .
