title: 163rd OG FY Chase Plane Support Services
description: Requirement: The 163d Attack Wing, California Air National Guard, located at March Air Reserve Base (KRIV), has issued Request for Quotation (RFQ) number W50S7427QA014 to secure professional, Chase Plane Support Services in support of Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPA) operations. This requirement is being competed as a Total Small Business Set-Aside and is conducted under the simplified procedures of FAR Subpart 12.2 (specifically FAR 12.201-1). The successful contractor will provide a dedicated, mission-capable chase aircraft, qualified pilot, and visual observer to accompany RPAs during flights outside of restricted airspace to ensure flight safety. Core Operational Requirements (PWS Reference) Aircraft Performance: Primary and back-up aircraft must sustain speeds of 150 knots true airspeed (KTAS) at altitudes of 12,000 feet and below. Communications: Dual-frequency radio capability to communicate on two separate frequencies simultaneously (RPA inter-plane and ATC). Onboard Equipment: Active beacons, strobe lights, and an FAA-compliant transponder capable of operating in "standby" mode with the assigned RPA formation code. Personnel Qualifications: Proposed pilots must hold FAA PIC ratings and current FAA Class 2 medicals. Proposed observers must hold current FAA Class 2 medicals. Both crew members must strictly comply with 14 CFR 91.17 (alcohol and drug use policy). Standby Responsiveness: Capability to arrive at designated handover points within 30 to 40 minutes of emergency/unscheduled notification. Basis of Award (LPTA): The Government intends to issue a single, firm-fixed-price purchase order to the responsible quoter whose quotation is determined to be Technically Acceptable, has Acceptable Past Performance, and offers the Lowest Total Evaluated Price (Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - LPTA). In accordance with FAR 12.203(c)(2), the evaluation process is highly streamlined. These procedures are strictly not subject to FAR Part 14 or Part 15. The Contracting Officer has broad discretion and is not required to establish a competitive range or use formal adjectival scoring. Quote Submission: Quoters must submit their quotations electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist. Quotations must be organized into four (4) separate volumes: Volume I � Technical Capability: Aircraft specifications, crew credentials, and operational standby plan (Maximum 10 pages; strictly no pricing). Volume II � Past Performance: Up to three (3) references for relevant contracts within the past three (3) years, including prime, subcontractor, or commercial experience (Maximum 3 pages). Volume III � Price: Completed firm-fixed-price CLIN schedule for the Base Period (1 Month) and five (5) Option Periods (1 Month each), fully burdened. Volume IV � Administrative: Signed SF 1449, completed Representations and Certifications, and active SAM.gov registration proof.

title: KC-130J � In-Flight Refueling Aircraft Parts & Equipment
description: 1 PROGRAM BACKGROUND: This sources sought is issued by the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD. The U.S. Marine Corp (USMC) and U.S. Navy Reserves (USNR) Tactical Air Lift Program (KC-130J Aircraft) PMA-207 is conducting a market survey of industry to determine potential interested sources that can provide In-Flight Refueling (IFR) aircraft pods, pods parts, fuse tank parts and equipment manufacturing; associated equipment including spares, repair parts, support equipment, technical manuals, training; and logistical engineering and field technical support. This market research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible vendors of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. Responses will also be utilized by the Government for market research purposes in developing its acquisition/contracting strategy. All interested parties must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) government website at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of Government contracts. This sources sought is used as a market research tool pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 to determine potential sources and their technical capabilities. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code currently assigned to this procurement is 336413 � Aircraft Auxiliary Parts. The product service code (PSC) is 1680 - Miscellaneous Aircraft Accessories and Components. title: C222--589-27-108, Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Building 26 KCVA (ME) FY27 NRM VISN Base - AE (VA-27-00021035)
description: DESCRIPTION Project: 589-27-108 Solicitation Number: 36C25527Q0057 RFP: 36C25527R0018 Title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Type of Notice: Sources Sought Posted Date:11/16/2026 Response Date: 12/1/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: C222 -Architect and Engineering- Electrical Systems NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for SF330's or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the VA Medical Center located in Kansas City, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 541330 Engineering Services and the size standard is $25.5 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail to matthew.finley@va.gov and received no later than December 1, 2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Business Opportunities website https://www.fbo.gov once available. Period of Performance for all design work is 150 calendar days including time for VA reviews. Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-75, the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73. The prime architect shall provide written certification of this to the Contracting Officer with the response provided for this market research. GENERAL SCOPE OF DESIGN: The Architect/Engineer (A/E)) shall provide professional design services for a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, uninterruptible power, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center (KCVA), 4801 Linwood Blvd, Kansas City, MO 64128. A/E Part One Services (also known as the design phase) for this design project encompass site visits as needed, field investigations, and the conduct of studies and user interviews to prepare detailed drawings, specifications, and cost estimates. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate and provide construction period services for a construction project. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center. The A/E services are required for preparation of Narrative, Studies, Phasing Design, Schematic Designs, Design Development, Construction Documents, and As Built Documents. The A/E shall coordinate all disciplines necessary to deliver a complete electrical infrastructure project. The A/E shall not rely solely on record drawings and shall verify existing conditions before using them as the basis of design. Ensuring all required permits and licenses from federal, state/provincial, or local authorities are obtained for the construction, installation, and operation of the equipment is also part of the A/E s responsibilities. The project design will comply with Infection Control and Interim Life Safety Measures. The A/E will provide design drawing, specification, and IGCE submissions at 35% (Schematic Design), 65% (Design Development), 95% (Construction Documents), and Final Bid Documents for all disciplines necessary to complete the project to the VA. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 541330 and qualified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned small business under NAICS code 541330. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 541330. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on December 21, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Project 589-27-108 Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26," IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://beta.sam.gov/. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs; Network 15 Contracting Office; 3450 S. 4th Street, Leavenworth, KS 66048 Point of Contact(s): Matt Finley, Contracting Officer, e-mail address: Matthew.Finley@va.gov

title: Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler, St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1284LL27Q0008 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler. Services and supplies are required for the currently installed tree cooler for the St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The tree cooler was built in 1984, the outdated HVAC system shall be replaced with a new HVAC system. The contractor shall provide a fully functioning new HVAC system for the existing tree cooler with associated evaporator fans and necessary materials for the refrigeration system. Contractor shall remove any humidifiers and associated parts, update the lighting, and install a notification system of a power outage due to ongoing power fluctuations. The contractor shall provide the personnel, materials, and equipment needed to perform the required services to industry standards and specifications. Representative shall communicate with POC regarding any issues that may arise. Contractor shall coordinate work hours with CO and COR for site access, hours, and operation. There will be no Government Property issued. Electricity will be available on site for Contractor's use. All work shall be completed by 03/15/2027. See attachment 1284LL27Q0008 for more details. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 811310 The small business size standard is $12.5 million dollars. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

title: Interactive Electronic Technical Manual LiveContent Viewer License
description: The United States Air Force (USAF) and Headquarters Air Mobility Command (HQ AMC) A4 established the requirement that all C-17 aircraft technical manuals (TM) will use the S1000D Specification Issue 4.0.2 or later versions of the technical data specification. Where cost-effective, the S1000D Issue 4.0.2 or later version will also be used to transform existing aircraft technical data to Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETM) Type Two format. The contractor shall maintain the authorized perpetual FMS LiveContent S1000D Standalone Consumer License � Per Land, Sea or Air Vehicle for the 29 C-17 aircraft. Annual maintenance support for all perpetual licenses shall be made available for a total of five years. An initial year shall be provided at contract award, with 4 additional one-year options. The total period of performance will be five years after contract award. The contractor shall provide five years of support services to assist in any technical difficulties that may arise and update the software via software updates, patches, or minor and major releases of new software at no additional cost to the customer. Initial support will be provided by TOMA personnel but any technical problems that cannot be remedied will be referred to RWS for corrective action.

description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) is seeking capability statements from all firms interested in a proposed training material development services Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. The following outline is recommended (5-page limit): 1) Company name, address, UEI (SAM), GSA contract # 2) A statement of capability which demonstrates the ability to perform this requirement. 3) Recent and relevant past performance information (Note: Prior government contract work is not required to submit a response.) USDA reserves the right to determine if a small business set-aside is appropriate based upon the capability information provided in response to this notice, and other pertinent information gathered by the contracting officer. Respondents should ensure the information provided is detailed, current, accurate, and complete. title: Scholarship Granting Organization (SGO) Program Administrator Support
description: NAVSUP FLCN Contracting Department BUMED/FM&C Directorate intends to procure program administrator services on behalf of the Department of War (DoW), through the Office of Military Community and Family Policy (MC&FP). This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number N0018927RB005 is issued as a request for proposal (RFP) for services as follows: General Summary & Program Objectives Program Intent: DoW, through the MC&FP, hereby establishes the Military Family Education Freedom Program. This initiative provides eligible active and Reserve Component Service members, DoW civilian employees, and military retirees with an authorized, voluntary after-tax payroll allotment pathway to direct contributions to a certified, Scholarship Granting Organization (SGO), as the Program Administrator. Tax Benefit Realization: In accordance with Internal Revenue Code (IRC) (S) 25F (enacted under Public Law 119-21), participating personnel are eligible to receive a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit of up to $1,700 annually ($3,400 for married couples filing jointly) for their qualified cash contributions. Mission-Critical Objective: The primary objective of this program is to enhance force readiness, retention, and quality of life for military-connected families by mitigating educational instability, establishing flexible K-12 schooling choices, and providing dedicated resources for special needs and transitional services. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. As stated above, offers shall be a certified SGO. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov.

title: Intent to Sole Source - Dredge Donnelly Operation Simulator
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT Notice ID: PANNAD-26-P-0000 032679/ W912BU-27-Q-A003 Department/Agency: USACE Philadelphia District Product Service Code (PSC): 6930 � Operation Training Devices NAICS Code: 333310 � Commercial and Service Industry Machinery Manufacturing Introduction and Background This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with RFO 5.101. This Notice does NOT constitute a request for competitive proposals, bids or quotes. The USACE Philadelphia District intends to award a contract on a noncompetitive basis under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(d) ("Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements"). Intended Awardee: IHC SMIT B.V. UEI: SZYEPF3FD2J1 CAGE Code: H2SY5 Address: Smitweg 6 , Kinderdijk 2961AW , Netherlands 2. Authority The proposed procurement is justified under the authority of 10 USC �3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1(d). This authority is applicable because RFO 6.103-1(d) allows for specification of attributes peculiar to one manufacturer in which the Dredge Donnelly Vessel Simulator is a product which requires the specification of attributes peculiar to one manufacturer: the designer of the Dredge DONNNELLY. 3. Description of Agency Requirement The supply to be furnished under this contract action is a custom hopper Dredge DONNELLY operating simulator that exactly mimics the actual controls and operation of the USACE hopper dredge DONNELLY. This procurement is necessary to fulfill the mission of the Dredge DONNELLY because the simulator will be used to train the DONNELLY crew. The simulator reacts in the same way the actual dredge would but in a simulated classroom style environment on multiple displays that match the view an operator would get if in the actual vessel�s pilothouse. The simulator must be developed based upon the actual layout of the controls on Dredge DONNELLY and actual functional response of those controls, as well as responses from sensors and alarms. External inputs to include specific geographic conditions, specific dredging conditions, and variable environmental and dredging conditions and parameters will be simulated. The simulator is a custom manufactured system utilizing the background design data from the hopper dredge itself, including the custom physical operator�s chair, which has control and monitoring capability built into it. In summary, the dredge simulator must exactly mimic the Dredge DONNELLY controls; these attributes are peculiar to one manufacturer: the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY. No other source has that information. 4. Justification for Sole Source IHC SMIT B.V. is the only responsible source to provide this dredge simulator and no other source will satisfy the Agency�s requirement because the specifications of the simulator require information and attributes that are particular and peculiar to only Royal IHC as the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY as set forth at RFO 6.103-1(d). As explained above, the simulator will be developed to exactly match the dredge operator�s station on the Dredge DONNELLY and exactly replicate the actual movements of the dredge based on the operator�s use of the simulator. IHC SMIT B.V.is the only company that has all of the information necessary to build a working functional simulator of the Dredge DONNELLY. That information includes, but is not limited to, the following: It has all the design background information related to this dredge; not only the physical layout, but all the engineering that has been produced and utilized in the background to include how the dredge will respond to various commands and how the dredge will display various alarms and malfunctions. It knows how all the vessel dredging components work, and how they interact. It knows the ranges of all the operating features and projected vessel reactions and performance. It has an extensive library of vessel operating parameters that can be altered to allow operators to change conditions in the simulation. It has the capability to integrate vessel operating simulation with geographical background simulation. As noted above, the simulator cannot be completed until the actual dredge itself goes through commissioning and all operational systems are finalized because they must match exactly. This reinforces why Royal IHC is the only responsible source who can produce the dredge simulator. In summary, the simulator requires specification of attributes peculiar to one manufacturer: the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY. This prevents full and open competition. No other source has access to the information required to produce the simulator. 5. Market Research Discussions were held with UASCE employee who manages the simulation laboratory at ERDC � USACE. Those discussions confirmed that the use of proprietary information running in the software for this simulator as well as the custom design of the operator�s station that exactly matches the station on the actual dredge make it impossible for anyone else to build the simulator specific to this application. It also builds in the exact operation of the dredge navigation and automation performance. While there are many organizations that can create simulators, they are all customized to specific operation being simulated and require the actual engineering of that operation and the items configuration and operating environment. Simple simulators display generic performance, but sophisticated simulators mimic the exact operation of the operation being simulated. They indicated that ERDC builds simulations for channel design based on general vessel performance input (turning radius, draft vessel size, etc.) Since channel design is their area of expertise, they have the background information needed and can design simulations for channel design. Keith reinforced that there are firms that could generate simulation software, but that without the background technical information and the specifics needed in this application, any simulation produced by others would include significant guesswork and only be of very limited value. 6. Conclusion IHC SMIT B.V. is the only responsible source to provide this dredge simulator and no other source will satisfy the Agency�s requirement because the specifications of the simulator require information and attributes that are particular and peculiar to only IHC SMIT B.V. as the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY as set forth at RFO 6.103-1(d). As explained above, the simulator will be developed to exactly match the dredge operator�s station on the Dredge DONNELLY and exactly replicate the actual movements of the dredge based on the operator�s use of the simulator.. title: NM FLAP SR35(1) Grant County Bridges
description: THIS IS NOT AN INVITIATION FOR BID, PLAN AND SPEFICIATIONS ARE NOT AVAILBLE PROJECT NUMBER: NM FLAP SR35(1) PROJECT NAME: GRANT COUNTY BRIDGES SET- ASIDE: FULL AND OPEN Competition with HUBZone Price Preference PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Grant County Bridges Project is located near Mimbres, New Mexico, in Grant County, along State Route (SR) 35. SR 35 serves as a 27?mile highway providing access to the Gila National Forest, connecting SR 15 in Silver City to SR 152 in Mimbres. The proposed improvements include work at four locations along SR 35: Bridge 1330 � Milepost (MP) 0.5 Concrete box culvert � MP 4.65 Bridge 1873 � MP 5.2 Bridge 1876 � MP 8.42 SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project includes reconstruction of three bridges and a concrete box culvert. Improvements would provide reliable and safe access to the Gila National Forest for local and regional travelers. Improvements to these structures would also benefit travelers by accessing residential and commercial properties along SR 35. Schedule A includes: The project includes demolition of the existing bridge and construction of three (3) new simple-span, precast, prestressed concrete bridges: an 80?ft simple span with precast prestressed I?girders and a cast?in?place reinforced concrete deck; a skewed 55?ft?6?in simple span using precast, prestressed voided slabs with a cast?in?place (CIP) concrete overlay; and a 36?ft simple span using precast, prestressed voided slabs with a cast?in?place (CIP) concrete overlay. Bridge 1, a 80?ft simple span: precast, prestressed I?girders with a cast?in?place reinforced concrete deck. Bridge 2, a 55?ft?6?in skewed simple span: precast, prestressed voided slabs with a cast?in?place (CIP) concrete overlay. Bridge 3, 36?ft simple span: precast, prestressed voided slabs with a cast?in?place (CIP) concrete overlay. Option X includes: The work consists of removing an existing open-bottom concrete box culvert and replacing it with a 10?ft by 5?ft reinforced concrete box culvert. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: Schedule A Removal of Bridge 484 Cuyd of Structural Concrete 707 LNFT of Precast, prestressed concrete slabs 48 inch voided (15� and 18�) 80,900 LB of reinforced steel epoxy coated 511 LNFT Bridge railing steel 800 LNFT drilled shaft 30 inches. 40 weeks of Temporary Traffic control flagger and Traffic Control Supervisor Option X 2 Each Concrete headwall (including wing walls) 60 LNFT, 10 ft span, 5 ft rise precast reinforced box culvert 5 weeks of Traffic Control Supervisor ESTIMATED COST RANGE: The estimated price range is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. ITEMS WORTH NOTING: Construction in Mimbres can be maintained through all seasons, but you must factor in cold-weather provisions for the winter months to ensure the integrity and quality of critical bridge and culvert materials like concrete and sealants.

title: Request for Information (RFI): Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) Project
description: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for sun/sky/lunar scanning photometers and replacement parts in support of the Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) in the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. AERONET is a global network of ground-based sun and sky-scanning radiometers that measures aerosol optical properties and precipitable water in near real time. NASA uses AERONET data to validate satellite aerosol retrievals and to maintain a uniform long-term record of aerosol properties. AERONET's installed base is more than 600 CE318-series photometers at land, ocean, and ship sites worldwide. The value of the network depends on standardized measurement, calibration, data format, and processing across every site. Any instrument added to the network must produce data that can be merged into the AERONET record and must work with the network's existing site infrastructure, including its tracking robots. The Government requires a contractor to supply both new sun/sky/lunar scanning photometers and replacement parts for the fielded fleet. New instruments are required in standard, polarization, and ocean-color configurations. They must automatically measure direct sun and lunar irradiance and diffuse sky radiance from 340 to 1640 nm; achieve a signal-to-noise ratio above 10,000:1 on all channels; transmit data through the NOAA/NESDIS Data Collection System (DCS), worldwide 4G/5G cellular networks, and PC/internet; run unattended on battery and 5-watt solar power; and operate sealed against rain, humidity, dust, and smoke from -20 to 50 degrees C. Replacement parts, such as sensor head cards, detectors, filters, collimators, CPU cards, modems, robot hardware, and gear reducer motor assemblies, must fit and work in NASA's fielded CE318-series instruments. NASA/GSFC is seeking capability statements from U.S. VENDORS ONLY, for the purposes of determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and level of competition for this requirement. For this RFI, a U.S. vendor is a firm organized under the laws of the United States or a U.S. state, with its principal place of business in the United States. NASA welcomes responses from U.S. manufacturers, authorized U.S. distributors, and other U.S. firms, including all socioeconomic categories of small business. Capability statements from foreign firms will not be reviewed. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small, 8(a), Women-owned (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-owned Small Business (EDWOSB), or HUBZone business set-aside based on responses received. Interested firms that possess the capability to meet the above requirement as described in the attached Statement of Work (SOW) are encouraged to submit a capability statement indicating the ability to meet all aspects of the requirement. NASA seeks input in the following areas: 1. Whether your firm is the manufacturer, an authorized distributor, or a reseller. Identify the manufacturer and country of manufacture for each item you would supply. 2. How your instruments meet the measurement, performance, communication, power, and environmental requirements in the SOW. If your instrument is not a CE318-series unit, explain how it would produce data compatible with the AERONET record, for example through side-by-side intercalibration results or use in AERONET or a similar federated network. 3. How your firm would supply replacement parts that fit and work in the fielded CE318-series units. 4. Your firm's experience supplying similar instruments or parts to government, research, or commercial customers in the past five years, with contract numbers and customer contacts. 5. Whether the items are commercial products as defined in FAR 2.101, and any applicable GSA Schedule or other government-wide contract vehicle. 6. Any requirement in the SOW that you believe unnecessarily limits competition, and what you would recommend instead. Each capability statement should also include the firm's name, address, Unique Entity ID (UEI), CAGE code, SAM.gov registration status, business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 334516, and a point of contact with name, title, phone, and email. All capability statements and RFI responses shall be submitted electronically via email to Contract Specialist Kermit Stanbach at kermit.s.stanbach@nasa.gov and Contracting Officer Cassandra Moore at cassandra.k.moore@nasa.gov no later than December 1, 2026, 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. Please reference Notice ID 80GSFC27Q0008 in any response. NASA intends to publicize a listing of respondents in order to facilitate teaming arrangements. Should your firm desire not to be included in this listing, clearly indicate this desire in your response.

title: UT NP ARCH 100(2) Bridges on Delicate Arch Road
description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 20420-0000 Embankment Construction: 10,000 CUYD 25101-0300 Placed Riprap, Class 3: 1,725 CUYD 30202-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 5,140 TON 40101-5600 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Gyratory Mix, 1/2-Inch or 3/4-Inch Nominal Maximum Size Aggregate, 0.3 To <3 Million ESAL: 8,300 TON 55201-0200 Structural Concrete, Class A (AE): 752 CUYD 55401-2000 Reinforcing Steel, Epoxy Coated: 138,000 LB 55601-1100 Bridge Railing, Steel, Two Rail: 642 LNFT 56501-0200 Drilled Shaft, 24-Inch Diameter: 750 LNFT 56501-0300 Drilled Shaft, 30-Inch Diameter: 890 LNFT 60901-1300 Curb, Concrete, 15-Inch Depth (Reinforced, Colored): 3,921 LNFT 61701-4500 Guardrail System Mgs, Type 2, Class A Steel Posts: 1,290 LNFT 63506-0500 Temporary Traffic Control, Flagger: 5,800 HOUR ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � September 2026 Award � November 2026 NTP � December 2026 Contract Completion � December 2028 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Total estimated cost between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 This will be solicited as a full and open competition.

title: J046--Water Tank Inspection & Disinfection
description: The Malcolm Randall VA Medical Center requires a one-time internal and external inspection of its 750,000-gallon water tower to satisfy the required five-year inspection cycle. Contractors are strongly encouraged to attend the site visit to evaluate site conditions and determine the resources, equipment, and personnel necessary to fulfill all requirements of this Statement of Work. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and incidentals necessary to perform a one-time five-year internal and external inspection, Water Tower Evaluation and Report, and Water Tower Washout and Disinfection in accordance with AWWA C652-11 for the 750,000-gallon water tower located at the Malcolm Randall VA Medical Center, 1601 SW Archer Road, Gainesville, FL 32608. All services shall be performed in accordance with the requirements of this Statement of Work.

title: 3D Image Reconstruction and Case Planning Services
description: The contractor shall provide services necessary to perform off-site Three Dimensional (3D) Image Reconstruction and Case Planning Services to eligible beneficiaries of North Florida/South Georgia VA Healthcare system, Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (hereinafter referred to as VAMC) off-site at the contractor�s facility. The specific services to be performed include the acquisition, upload and assessment of quality of digital Computerized Tomography (CT) Scan images, multiplanar reformatting of digital data, and production of a 3D reconstruction tool for use in case planning for endovascular procedures. The contractor shall provide 3D Image Reconstruction and Case Planning services in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS).

title: Request For Proposal (RFP) for NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium
description: Update 11/13/2026 The purpose of this announcement is to publish Amendment 0003 to Solicitation 80KSC024R0010 for the 2027 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In (Amendment 0001 and Amendment 0002 were posted with the origninal solicitation), extend the proposal due date from November 20, 2026, to December 1, 2026, and provide Questions and Answers. See attached 80KSC024R0010 Amendment 0003 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In and 80KSC024R0010 2027 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In Questions and Answers. ____________________________________________________________________ UPDATE 10/20/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium opt-in opportunity as described in the original Helium Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.10, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium RFP was issued on December 21, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium contract's ordering period remains valid through September 30, 2030. The RFP has resulted in the award of four fixed-price indefinite delivery (ID) requirements contracts to supply liquid and gaseous helium in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. Awards were made to the following companies: Airgas USA LLC (South), Airgas USA LLC (West), Linde, Inc., and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing helium contractors for each additional IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant is a company that does not currently hold a NASA liquid and gaseous helium contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government's determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing helium Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.10 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. The commodities will support current and future aerospace flight, simulation, research, development, testing, and other operations at the following NASA centers and facilities: Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF) locations (Palestine, TX, Ft Sumner, NM, Port Hueneme, CA, and Burns, OR); Glenn Research Center (GRC), Cleveland, OH 44135; GRC Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (GRC-ATF), Sandusky, OH 44870; Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD 20771; Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Pasadena, CA 91109; Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston, TX 77058; Kennedy Space Center (KSC - including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station - CCSFS); Langley Research Center (LaRC), Hampton, VA 23666; Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, AL, 35812; Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF), New Orleans, LA 70129; Stennis Space Center (SSC), Stennis Space Center, MS, 39529; White Sands Test Facility (WSTF), Las Cruces, NM 88012; and other such places of performance as required in this contract. Submission information: 1. Opt-in by a Current Helium Contractor. A current Helium Contractor shall submit Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. If the Contractor is determined technically acceptable, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). 2. Opt-in by New Entrant. The new entrant shall submit an Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. Once determined acceptable from a technical standpoint, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). New entrants will be required to comply with provisions in Section 5 of the RFP and all terms and conditions of the resulting contract. 3. All questions regarding this opt-in notice shall be submitted in writing via email to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. The Government will not answer oral questions due to the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation. The Offeror shall submit all questions, if any, no later than November 4, 2026, to allow for analysis and dissemination of responses in advance of the proposal due date. The Government will not guarantee a response to late questions. Questions shall not be directed to the technical activity personnel. 4. It is requested that any interested party notify the helium Contracting Officers via email no later than November 4, 2026, of your intent to submit a proposal during this opt-in period as well as the name(s) of which NASA Center(s) you intend to propose. Please send your notice of intent to propose to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. 5. All offers shall be sent to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov by November 20, 2026, by 4:30PM EST. Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, paragraph (f). 6. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition is Marcus Orr, Acting Deputy Procurement Officer at marcus.c.orr@nasa.gov. ************************************** Amendment 0002. Also attached is the Questions and Responses to RFP document. ********************************************************************************************** The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. buyer: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH (HZB)
title: Germany – Laboratory furniture – V456_2026 - HiPOLE - Laborausstattung inkl. Planung (Lab2Fab)
description: Als eines von 18 Zentren der Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft beschäftigt das Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie (HZB) rund 1.400 Mitarbeiter an den Standorten Berlin-Wannsee und Berlin-Adlershof – und verfügt über einen Gesamthaushalt von zirka 110 Millionen Euro. Das HZB arbeitet eng mit den Universitäten und Fachhochschulen in Berlin-Brandenburg zusammen. Das HZB forscht an Lösungen für eine klimaneutrale Gesellschaft. Forschende entwickeln und optimieren effiziente und preiswerte Materialien für Solarzellen, Batterien und Katalysatoren. Diese Energiematerialien sind wesentliche Bausteine auf dem Weg in eine CO2-neutrale und sichere Energieversorgung. Wichtigstes Werkzeug ist die Röntgenquelle BESSY II, welche intensives Licht im weichen Röntgenbereich liefert. Damit wird der Aufbau von Energie- und Quantenmaterialien sowie ihre Funktionsweise untersucht. Das HZB forscht auch an neuen Konzepten für beschleunigerbasierte Röntgenquellen und entwickelt neue Instrumente mit immer höheren Messgenauigkeiten. Das HZB und die Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena gründeten 2023 das Helmholtz-Institut für Polymere in Energieanwendungen (HIPOLE) in Jena als dauerhafte Einrichtung des HZB. Führende Expertisen in den Bereichen Energiespeicherung und Photovoltaik, polymere Materialien, künstliche Intelligenz sowie nachhaltige Chemie konnten somit gebündelt werden, um die beschleunigte wissensbasierte Erforschung nachhaltiger Polymermaterialien für skalierbare Energietechnologien voranzubringen. HIPOLE Jena basiert auf drei Forschungssäulen: • Materialdesign und Synthese • Skalierbarkeit, Prototypen und Transfer sowie • Charakterisierung, Theorie, Modellierung und Datenwissenschaften. Der Fokus liegt nicht nur in der Grundlagenforschung, sondern auch im Transfer der Forschungsergebnisse. Aktuell sind an HIPOLE Jena rund 50 Mitarbeitende beschäftigt. Die Forschungsarbeiten der Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler am HIPOLE Jena, unterstützt von sieben assoziierten Mitgliedern der FSU Jena und des HZB, lassen sich fünf Forschungsbereichen zuordnen: 1. Polymere Redox-Flow Batterien, 2. Polymer-basierte Dünnschichtbatterien, 3. Photovoltaik, 4. Funktionale selbstheilende Materialien und 5. Nachhaltige Chemie. Das Helmholtz-Institut für Polymere in Energieanwendungen Jena (HIPOLE Jena) beabsichtigt die Beschaffung von Laborausstattung inkl. Planung (Lab2Fab). Es sollen drei Laborräume mit Labormöbeln in bezugsfertigen Laborflächen im Lab2Fab in Jena ausgestattet werden.

Paslaugų apimtis: Visų privalomųjų tyrimų parengimas; Projektinių pasiūlymų parengimas, visuomenės informavimas (apmoka projektuotojas); Statybą leidžiančio dokumento gavimas; Techninio darbo ir Tvarkybos darbų projektų parengimas. Techninis darbo projektas: • Bendroji dalis; • Sklypo plano dalis; • Architektūrinė dalis; • Konstrukcijų dalis; • Elektrotechnikos apšvietimas dalis; • Elektrotechnikos dalis (ESO) (pagal poreikį); • Paveldosaugos dalis; • Apsauginės signalizacijos, stebėjimo kameros; • Pasirengimo statybai ir statybos darbų organizavimo dalis; • Statybos skaičiuojamosios kainos nustatymo dalis. • Kitos būtinos dalys, kurias, įvertinęs projektuojamų statinių specifiką, specialiuosius, reikalavimus ir prisijungimo sąlygas, Projektuotojas suderina su Statytoju (Užsakovu). Tvarkybos darbų projektas – vertingųjų savybių, nurodytų kultūros vertybės aprašyme: ● mažosios kraštovaizdžio architektūros statinių ir vaizduojamojo meno formų statyba / /atnaujinimas/atkūrimas, ● takų, kelių ar jų dangų statyba/atkūrimas, ● želdynų ir želdinių tvarkymas, ● hidrotechninių įrenginių statyba/atkūrimas. title: Finland – Maintenance of information technology software – Rajatarkastussovelluksen (Ratas) ylläpidon hankinta
description: Rajavartiolaitos (myöhemmin myös Hankintayksikkö) kilpailuttaa Ratas-järjestelmän ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelut. Ratas-järjestelmä on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 "ylläpidettävän kohteen kuvaus". Ratas on käytössä oleva tietojärjestelmäkokonaisuus, jonka toiminnan jatkuvuus, käytettävyys, tietoturvallisuus ja hallittu kehittäminen ovat keskeisiä hankintayksikön toiminnan kannalta. Järjestelmää on kehitetty vaiheittain nykyisen toimintamallin mukaisesti. Tulevan kilpailutuksen tavoitteena on muodostaa pitkäjänteinen palvelumalli, jolla varmistetaan järjestelmän laadukas ylläpito sekä mahdollistetaan tarpeelliset muutokset ja jatkokehitys hallitusti. Hankinnan ensisijaisena tavoitteena on varmistaa: • järjestelmän jatkuva käytettävyys ja toimintavarmuus • tehokas häiriönhallinta ja ongelmanratkaisu • järjestelmän teknisen ympäristön ylläpito • tietoturvallinen ja hallittu muutosten toteuttaminen • tarvittavan dokumentaation ja osaamisen säilyminen • tilaajan tukeminen järjestelmän elinkaaren hallinnassa. Palvelu sisältää alustavasti seuraavia kokonaisuuksia: Ylläpitopalvelut • järjestelmän jatkuva ylläpito • häiriöiden vastaanotto, analysointi ja ratkaisu • palvelupyyntöjen käsittely • ongelmanhallinta • versio- ja muutostenhallinta • käyttöympäristön tekninen ylläpito • yhteistyö infrastruktuuri- ja muiden toimittajien kanssa. Sovellustuki ja tekninen hallinta • sovelluksen teknisen toiminnan varmistaminen • sovelluskomponenttien hallinta • tekninen selvitys- ja asiantuntijatuki • suorituskyvyn ja kapasiteetin seuranta • tietoturvallisuuden ylläpito. Jatkokehitys ja muutokset • pienimuotoiset kehitystoimenpiteet • korjaavat ja ennakoivat muutokset • toiminnalliset kehitystarpeet • tekninen velanhallinta. Varsinainen kehitystyö ei ole hankinnan pääasiallinen tavoite, vaan sen tarkoituksena on tukea järjestelmän elinkaaren hallintaa ja ylläpitopalvelun onnistumista. Jatkokehityksen osuus palvelussa on ylläpitoa täydentävä osa-alue. Sen tavoitteena on mahdollistaa tarvittavat muutokset, korjaukset ja rajatut kehitystarpeet ilman erillisiä raskaita järjestelyjä. Ratas-järjestelmää on tarkoitus jatkokehittää tulevien vuosien aikana integraatiolla European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) -järjestelmään ja uusimalla Ratas-järjestelmän käyttäjätunnistus nykyaikaisella ratkaisulla. Osallistumispyynnön tavoitteena on tunnistaa markkinoilta rajattu määrä ehdokkaita, joilla on riittävä osaaminen ja kapasiteetti vastata Ratas-järjestelmän ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelusta. Ratas-järjestelmä tullaan korvaamaan nykyisen suunnitelman mukaan ensi vuosikymmenen puolella. Korvaavan järjestelmän hankinnan yksityiskohdat ovat vielä päättämättä.

description: Предметът на обществената поръчка е „Доставка на оптически прибори, чрез сключване на рамкови споразумения по три самостоятелно обособени позиции“, както следва: Обособена позиция № 1 „Доставка на монокуляр за нощно виждане ”, съгласно ТС О 33.4578.24 – ВО; Обособена позиция № 2 „Доставка на нощен оптически мерник за стрелково оръжие“, съгласно ТС О 33.4579.24 – ВО; Обособена позиция № 3 „Доставка на дневен оптически мерник“, съгласно ТС О 33.4927.25 – ВО. Обществената поръчка не съдържа класифицирана информация по смисъла на § 2, т. 20 от Допълнителните разпоредби на ЗОП. В Рамковите споразумения са определени всички условия и на основание чл. 82, ал. 1 от ЗОП, Възложителят ще сключва конкретни договори, като прилага тези условия. - По Обособена позиция № 1 „Доставка на монокуляр за нощно виждане ”, съгласно ТС О 33.4578.24 – ВО - общото прогнозно количество, което се предвижда да бъде доставено до 2960 броя, разпределена (прогнозно) по години за целия срок на действие на рамковото споразумение. - По Обособена позиция № 2 „Доставка на нощен оптически мерник за стрелково оръжие“, съгласно ТС О 33.4579.24 – ВО - общото прогнозно количество, което се предвижда да бъде доставено до 1228 броя, разпределена (прогнозно) по години за целия срок на действие на рамковото споразумение. - По Обособена позиция № 3 „Доставка на дневен оптически мерник“, съгласно ТС О 33.4927.25 – ВО - общото прогнозно количество, което се предвижда да бъде доставено е до 1439 броя, разпределена (прогнозно) по години за целия срок на действие на рамковото споразумение.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Rosebud Lift Station Construction
description: The existing lift station has been in place since the early 1990s. Since its creation the hospital anticipates increased expansion in the emergency department, added on Tribal programs (dialysis, detox, Tribal Health Administration Building), added on 19 more quarters units, and is anticipating adding an additional 23 quarters units. The existing pumps are facing replacement every 1-2 years due to the unanticipated growth, but due to the growth we need to consider increasing the capacity of the wet well. In addition to switching from standard submersible pumps to chopper pumps to accommodate the random objects that get flushed into the system. In July both pumps ended up failing and they had to not only replace the pumps but pay for sewage disposal to circumvent overflow. A separate project is in the works to begin remediating/replacing damaged sewer mains due to inflow and infiltration. This construction solicitation will require the full removal and replacement of the lift station for the Rosebud complex. The existing lift station provides wastewater service to the hospital quarters units, and several tribal program buildings. Once installation is complete the new lift station will take the full sanitary load for the area currently being serviced by the existing lift station and be sized to handle expansion in the future. Then the existing lift station consisting of the wet well, dry well, pumps and piping will be demolished. The new lift station will consist of a wet well, a dry well, installation of chopper pumps, and force main connection. This project will also include a new control system to allow the facility to monitor flow into the lift station and the status of the equipment. Brand Names: Where brand names are referenced, they establish a standard of quality and performance. Offerors may propose equal products that meet or exceed the specified functional and performance requirements. The Government will evaluate equality based on technical compatibility, performance, and integration with the system.

title: $300M Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) Program at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Sources Sought Notice and Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). There are no bid packages, solicitations, specifications, or drawings available with this announcement. It does not constitute a procurement commitment by USACE, implied or otherwise. No contract will be awarded from this Sources Sought Notice. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. No reimbursement will be made for any cost associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow-up information requests. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal if a solicitation is issued in the future. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential contractors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to contractors regarding their submissions. Additional information may be requested after initial response, either from individual respondents or all respondents. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market research to support acquisition of an estimated $300M MATOC to support Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) construction efforts. This Market Research will help USACE determine the availability and capabilities of firms working within this NAICS code. The responses to this Notice will also be used to help determine whether a small business or socio-economic set-aside may be suitable to apply to this potential procurement. 3. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The purpose of this MATOC will be to support primarily general construction activities at JBLM and its sub-installations (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center), including but not limited to renovation, repairs, minor building expansions and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), preventative maintenance, environmental abatement, erosion control and earthwork. The JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities. Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM. Task Orders under this MATOC are primarily intended to provide a timely procurement response to general construction work such as remediation of facilities, e.g., maintenance, repair, asbestos and lead-based paint abatement, and minor construction situations relating to but not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and anti-terrorism and force protection. Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. The MATOC may also be used for Task Orders expected to require some Incidental Design Work or extension of design effort by the Contractor, to include, but not be limited to fire alarm systems, fire sprinkler systems, HVAC system installation and balancing, communications systems, structural design of minor facilities or components and licensed professional engineer certification of site adaptation of pre-engineered structures. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The USACE Seattle District intends to award a MATOC to offerors determined to be qualified in accordance with the evaluation criteria. Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $300 Million ordering capacity, shared among all MATOC contractors. Structure: Qualified firms will be issued a MATOC contract, establishing a pool of multiple contractors available to support JBLM FSRM. Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with a single two (2) year option period. Exercise of options is at the Government's discretion. Project Size and Task Order Limits: The project size for Task Orders under this MATOC are anticipated to be between $250,000.00 and $25,000,000.00, and the average project duration is expected to be between six months to two years. Based on previous similar contracts, the occurrence of Task Orders may be frequent, especially in emergency situations, and during the 3rd and 4th quarters of the Government�s fiscal year. Project Delivery Methods: Projects will primarily be executed using Design-Bid-Build project delivery, with task orders representing the construction portion of project delivery. Task Order Selection: Competition for task orders will be held among all MATOC participants. Source selection methods will be determined for individual projects and may include various prices, performance, schedule or other trade-offs on the best-value spectrum. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the JBLM area on or about 15 October 2026. Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI) later. Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/k6LtDRMKPP The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market research needed for determining the number and availability of contractors interested in this acquisition. Interested parties are also asked to submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 20 September 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. John McGuire, Contract Specialist Jeffrey Ross, Contracting Officer JBLM Special Projects Branch Contracting Division, Seattle District, Northwestern Division Email: john.e.mcguire@usace.army.mil Subject line: �Sources Sought Response � JBLM FSRM MATOC $300M � [Firm Name]� The Government welcomes candid industry feedback, recommendations, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this program. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

description: AMENDMENT 0001 TO SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE The purpose of this amendment is to announce that an Industry Day will not be held for this requirement due to the high level of interest received in response to the Sources Sought notice. Prospective contractors should continue to monitor SAM.gov for all updates pertaining to this requirement. 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Sources Sought Notice and Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). There are no bid packages, solicitations, specifications, or drawings available with this announcement. It does not constitute a procurement commitment by USACE, implied or otherwise. No contract will be awarded from this Sources Sought Notice. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. No reimbursement will be made for any cost associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow-up information requests. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal if a solicitation is issued in the future. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential contractors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to contractors regarding their submissions. Additional information may be requested after initial response, either from individual respondents or all respondents. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market research to support acquisition of an estimated $300M MATOC to support Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) construction efforts. This Market Research will help USACE determine the availability and capabilities of firms working within this NAICS code. The responses to this Notice will also be used to help determine whether a small business or socio-economic set-aside may be suitable to apply to this potential procurement. 3. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The purpose of this MATOC will be to support primarily general construction activities at JBLM and its sub-installations (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center), including but not limited to renovation, repairs, minor building expansions and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), preventative maintenance, environmental abatement, erosion control and earthwork. The JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities. Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM. Task Orders under this MATOC are primarily intended to provide a timely procurement response to general construction work such as remediation of facilities, e.g., maintenance, repair, asbestos and lead-based paint abatement, and minor construction situations relating to but not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and anti-terrorism and force protection. Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. The MATOC may also be used for Task Orders expected to require some Incidental Design Work or extension of design effort by the Contractor, to include, but not be limited to fire alarm systems, fire sprinkler systems, HVAC system installation and balancing, communications systems, structural design of minor facilities or components and licensed professional engineer certification of site adaptation of pre-engineered structures. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The USACE Seattle District intends to award a MATOC to offerors determined to be qualified in accordance with the evaluation criteria. Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $300 Million ordering capacity, shared among all MATOC contractors. Structure: Qualified firms will be issued a MATOC contract, establishing a pool of multiple contractors available to support JBLM FSRM. Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with a single two (2) year option period. Exercise of options is at the Government's discretion. Project Size and Task Order Limits: The project size for Task Orders under this MATOC are anticipated to be between $250,000.00 and $25,000,000.00, and the average project duration is expected to be between six months to two years. Based on previous similar contracts, the occurrence of Task Orders may be frequent, especially in emergency situations, and during the 3rd and 4th quarters of the Government�s fiscal year. Project Delivery Methods: Projects will primarily be executed using Design-Bid-Build project delivery, with task orders representing the construction portion of project delivery. Task Order Selection: Competition for task orders will be held among all MATOC participants. Source selection methods will be determined for individual projects and may include various prices, performance, schedule or other trade-offs on the best-value spectrum. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the JBLM area on or about 15 October 2026. Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI) later. Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. description: The purpose of this Amendment 01 to Request for Quote (RFQ) F41999-27-Q-0007 for the AFSVC PACA Audit is to as follows: 1.PACA Audit RFQ F41999-27-Q-0007 - Questions & Answers are hereby added to the solicitation. 2.Offeror Letter - PACA Special Audits (13NOV26) is hereby replaced with Offeror Letter - PACA Special Audits (17NOV26). 3.ATCH 01 Instructions to Contractors (3NOV26) is hereby replaced with ATCH 01 Instructions to Contractors (17NOV26). 4.ATCH 14 is now the PACA Audit RFI Questions & Answers 5.ATCH 15 NAF Standard Clauses Incorporated By Reference Full Text 30 May 2025 is hereby added to the solicitation. 6.The solicitation closing date is hereby changed from Monday, 23 November 2026, 4:00 PM CT to now read: Tuesday, 1 December 2026, 4:00 PM CT. Please acknowledge receipt of this Amendment 01 below & return it in your File #1 Contract Documentation. General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Specific Focus Areas for the PACA Special Audits Program: � A. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. Scope Air Force Services Center requires the audit services of licensed Certified Public Accountants (CPAs) or CPA firms to perform financial statement audits of Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) financial statements and performance audits of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Services activities, with particular emphasis on high-risk areas identified through preliminary risk assessments and annual selection matrices.
