title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] and each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: �

Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] and each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: �

description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIRSYSCOM), acting under the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS) at Patuxent River, MD, intends to compete and award a limited source Firm Fixed Price (FFP) type Delivery Order. This order will be competed under one of four existing Basic Ordering Agreements (BOAs) to the below vendors for the procurement of Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Maritime Services: N0001925G1000: Insitu, Inc. title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar Creech AFB, Nevada Progressive Design-Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: DESCRIPTION The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Los Angeles District, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) / Market Intelligence Notice to obtain industry feedback regarding the anticipated design and construction of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada, using Progressive Design-Build (PDB) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Other Transaction Authority for Construction. The purpose of this notice is to gather market intelligence regarding industry capabilities, experience, commercial practices, acquisition considerations, and potential challenges associated with the proposed project. Information obtained through this notice will assist the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, identifying potential industry participants, and refining project requirements prior to the release of the formal Program Solicitation. This notice is issued for informational and acquisition planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government to award an agreement. I. PURPOSE OF MARKET INTELLIGENCE USACE is conducting preliminary market intelligence to better understand industry capabilities and obtain feedback regarding the proposed use of Progressive Design-Build under an Other Transaction framework. The Government is particularly interested in receiving information regarding industry experience with progressive design-build delivery, design and construction of specialized military aviation facilities, anticipated project risks, acquisition considerations, and commercial practices that may improve project delivery. Participation in this market intelligence effort is voluntary. Responses will be used solely to support acquisition planning and development of the Government's proposed acquisition approach. II. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar Creech AFB, Nevada Project Location: Creech Air Force Base, Nevada Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Los Angeles District Program Amount (est.): $180M - $200M NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M Project Delivery Method: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) Acquisition Authority: 10 U.S.C. � 2808a � Other Transaction Authority for Construction III. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The proposed project consists of the design and construction of a Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar facility at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada. The project is anticipated to provide an approximately 84,931-square-foot facility consisting of a squadron command and operations center, aircraft maintenance unit, hangar bay, and associated aircraft parking apron to support CCA operations and aircraft maintenance activities. The project may include associated site improvements, utilities, infrastructure, and supporting facilities necessary to provide a complete and functional operational facility. The preliminary scope of work is subject to further development and refinement. Additional project requirements and technical information may be provided in future acquisition announcements. IV. ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION APPROACH The Government is considering the use of Progressive Design-Build (PDB) under the Other Transaction Authority for Construction pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Under the proposed approach, the Government anticipates utilizing a streamlined competitive selection process consisting of the following steps: Step 1 � White Papers / Statements of Qualifications Interested parties would submit qualification information demonstrating relevant experience, technical capabilities, management approach, and qualifications to perform the proposed project. Following evaluation of the submissions, the Government anticipates selecting a limited number of highly qualified firms to proceed to the next step. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations Selected firms would be invited to participate in pitch presentations to further demonstrate their qualifications, technical approach, and ability to successfully execute the proposed project. The Government anticipates selecting a preferred Progressive Design-Build Entity (PDBE) for negotiations regarding the initial agreement. Anticipated Post-Award Approach The proposed PDB approach would generally include two phases: Phase 1 � Design Development and Preconstruction Services: Collaborative development and refinement of the design, project requirements, construction approach, cost estimates, schedule, and associated preconstruction activities. Phase 2 � Final Design and Construction: Completion of the remaining design and construction activities, subject to successful negotiations, required approvals, and availability of funds. The final selection process, agreement structure, pricing methodology, and contractual arrangements will be established in the formal Program Solicitation and applicable agreement documents. V. MARKET INTELLIGENCE REQUESTED The Government is seeking input from interested industry participants regarding the proposed project and acquisition approach. Interested parties are encouraged to provide responses to the following questions: 1. Company Information and Capabilities Provide the company name, business address, primary point of contact, and a brief description of the firm's capabilities relevant to the proposed project. 2. Relevant Project Experience Describe your firm's experience with Progressive Design-Build or similar collaborative project delivery methods, particularly for military aviation facilities, hangars, or other complex construction projects. Also describe your firm�s (or proposed team�s) experience designing and constructing ICD 705-compliant spaces, including accreditation support. 3. Progressive Design-Build / OTA Experience Has your firm participated in projects utilizing Progressive Design-Build or Other Transaction agreements? If so, briefly describe your experience and identify any lessons learned. 4. Proposed Acquisition Strategy Does your firm have any recommendations or concerns regarding the proposed two-step selection process consisting of White Papers and Pitch Presentations? 5. Project Delivery and Risk Considerations What significant technical, design, construction, logistical, or scheduling challenges should the Government consider when developing the project requirements and acquisition strategy? Specifically address the following: Site-Specific Realities: Creech AFB is a remote desert location characterized by extreme temperatures, specialized airspace/base access constraints, and limited local labor and material resources. Key Drivers: Identify the primary cost and schedule drivers you foresee for this project. Mitigation Strategies: Describe your recommended risk mitigation and sourcing strategies to overcome these challenges. 6. Pricing and Commercial Practices What pricing approaches, cost development methods, and commercial practices would your firm recommend for a Progressive Design-Build agreement involving design development and subsequent construction? 7. Industry Participation Would your firm be interested in participating in the anticipated competition? If not, please identify any significant barriers to participation. 8. Additional Recommendations Provide any additional recommendations that may assist the Government in refining the project requirements, improving competition, managing risks, or developing the proposed PDB w/ OTA acquisition strategy. VI. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are encouraged to submit written responses addressing the market intelligence questions identified in Section V. Responses should be concise and limited to information relevant to the proposed project and acquisition approach. Respondents are requested to identify any proprietary or confidential business information included in their submissions. The Government may use information received to support acquisition planning and development of future requirements. No evalua

title: NOMEC and NOPP Partnership Forum
description: Request for Information (RFI) THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and market research planning purposes; it does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation. Furthermore, those who respond to this RFI should not anticipate feedback with regards to its submission; other than acknowledgment of receipt - ONLY IF a request for an acknowledgement is requested by the submitter. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is not seeking proposals at this time. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. All submissions become the property of the Federal Government, and will not be returned. Purpose of this RFI: The purpose of this RFI is to obtain detailed information from interested members of the public regarding opportunities to strengthen cross-sector partnerships in support of U.S. ocean mapping, exploration, and characterization priorities. Responses to this Request for Information (RFI) will inform development of the National Ocean Mapping, Exploration, and Characterization (NOMEC) and National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP) Partnership Forum on Building U.S. Ocean Technology and Data Partnerships to Advance Ocean Mapping, Exploration, and Characterization. In particular, the NOMEC Council and NOPP seek information regarding stakeholder priorities and capabilities; barriers to effective collaboration with the Federal Government; opportunities for enhanced cross-sector partnerships; and topics and activities that could support actionable outcomes from the Forum. NOAA is specifically looking for input as follows: Provide a high-level overview of your response to the attached document. This summary should articulate understanding of the RFI's primary objective and briefly outline the nature of the information, product, service, or capability being described. Describe the specialized technical teams, intellectual property (IP), or unique resources that would support the capabilities described in the attached document. Specified responses are requested in regards to Questions 1 through 9 of the attached document: Reference Question # - specific question or area of interest Respondent�s comprehensive response and detailed answer Please see the attached Attachment 1 Request for Information for specifics. Submission of Information: Interested parties are encouraged to submit a response which supports their claim that they have the qualifications and experience to provide services for one or more of the identified services. If there are areas of the requirement that your company and/or prospective team cannot meet, please identify those areas in your response along with amplifying information as to why your team cannot meet the government�s request. Specifically, any interested parties should provide the following information: Name of Company, address, and SAM.gov Unique Entity (UEID); Business type and designation (i.e., large business, small business, socioeconomic designation); Point of contact name, email, and phone number; Company website address; Any General Service Administration (GSA) schedule, Government Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), or Multiple Award Contract numbers and information that may allow for streamlined procurement of services from your company; Do you currently have a contract(s) with any other Federal Agency for these types of services? Do you have a commercial catalog of products or systems similar to these services? RFI Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of submittals to this RFI, respondents are encouraged to prepare a response that closely adheres to the following format: The document format shall be either Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx), or Adobe Acrobat (.pdf) formats. Responses shall be prepared using 12 pt. font, 1-inch margins, and 8.5� by 11� paper and shall not exceed twenty (20) pages in length, including images, data displays, charts, graphs, and tables. It should be noted in the messaging of this RFI that participants should focus on their area of expertise to allow for diversity in responses. Respondents are encouraged to include any supporting material, such as data sheets or previous mission reports, as a separate attachment. Any such supporting material will be excluded from the page count. Response Deadline and Point of Contact Information: Responses to this notice should be documents attached to emails with the subject line �RFI Response - NOMEC and NOPP Partnership Forum� received no later than 3:00PM MT, Tuesday, December 1, 2026 to: Contract Specialist, Julia Hamilton at julia.l.hamilton@noaa.gov Contracting Officer, Angela Royster at angela.royster@noaa.gov The responses received will assist NOAA with identifying feasible technical solutions for this requirement. Each respondent, by submitting a response, agrees that any cost incurred by it in responding to this request, or in support of activities associated with this RFI, shall be the sole responsibility of the respondent. NOAA shall incur no obligations or liabilities whatsoever, to anyone, for any costs or expenses incurred by the respondent in responding to this RFI. Responses to this RFI will not be returned. Industry Discussions: Some respondents may be asked to provide additional information regarding the matters addressed in this RFI. Those respondents will be contacted directly if there is a need for further information. Questions: Respondents may submit questions regarding this RFI to the contact(s) listed above. Responses to questions may be posted on the Government Point of Entry. Please send any questions you may have to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer by no later than (NLT) 3:00PM MST, Friday, November 13, 2026. Each question shall provide the question number of the particular item being referred to in this RFI.

title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. title: Germany – Construction work – DSP - Pumpenhaus Scharnhorststraße Dezentral
description: Das Projekt DSP – Dezentral Scharnhorststraße Pumpenhaus ist eine Infrastrukturmaßnahme zur Erweiterung und Modernisierung des Heizwerks Scharnhorststraße. Am Standort Scharnhorststraße wird eine neue Wärmeübertragerstation mit zwei Pumpengruppen, Rohrleitungssystemen sowie den erforderlichen elektro- und leittechnischen Einrichtungen in einer „Brownfield-Umgebung“ errichtet. Die Umsetzung erfolgt innerhalb eines bestehenden Heizwerksstandortes in einer Brownfield-Umgebung. Neben der Errichtung neuer Anlagenkomponenten sind zahlreiche Schnittstellen zu bestehenden Anlagen, Rohrleitungssystemen, elektro- und leittechnischen Einrichtungen sowie betrieblichen Prozessen zu berücksichtigen. Besonderes Augenmerk liegt dabei auf der Aufrechterhaltung der Versorgungssicherheit und die Umsetzung aller relevanten Umschlussarbeiten innerhalb eines drei (3) monatigen Stillstandsfensters. Für die Umsetzung des Projektes werden in einem vorgelagerten Projekt bereits die erforderlichen Voraussetzungen zur Baufeldfreimachung geschaffen. Aufbauend darauf umfasst das Projekt DSP die Ausführungsplanung, Beschaffung, Errichtung, Inbetriebsetzung und Übergabe der neuen Anlagentechnik einschließlich aller hierfür erforderlichen Nebenleistungen. Auszuführende Arbeiten: • Montage und Umbau von Fernwärme-Anlagenkomponenten • Installation und Integration von Pumpensystemen mit elektrischer Antriebstechnik • Rohrleitungsbau für Fernwärmeanwendungen einschließlich Verbindung und Einbindung von Anlagenteilen (Nennweiten ca. DN 200 bis DN 600) • Anbindung neuer Rohrleitungen und Komponenten an bestehende Versorgungs- und Rohrleitungssysteme • Lieferung und Montage von Armaturen, Regel- und Absperreinrichtungen (Nennweiten ca. DN 250 bis DN 600) • Planung und Errichtung von Rohrleitungsbefestigungen sowie unterstützenden Stahlbaukonstruktionen • Einbindung bestehender Anlagenkomponenten in neu errichtete Systeme • Herstellung von Fundamenten für Anlagen- und Stahlbaukomponenten • Anpassung und Erweiterung von Niederspannungs-, Energieversorgungs- und Antriebssystemen • Anpassung und Erweiterung von Mess-, Steuerungs- und Leittechnik • Erneuerung elektrischer Energieversorgungsanlagen einschließlich Kabelverlegung • Demontage und Rückbau bestehender Anlagen- und Rohrleitungskomponenten (Nennweiten bis ca. DN 500) Die Anbindungen an das Netz erfolgen auf dem Betriebsgelände. Die oberirdische Zuführung der beiden DN500 Leitungen auf dem Betriebsgelände auf einem bestehenden Stahlbau gehört zum Projektumfang. Die vorhandene und zu erweiternde Leittechnik ist auf dem Betriebsgebäude verortet. Die Planung der E- und Leittechnik sind Bestandteil vom Projektumfang. Schnittstellen zur bestehenden E- und Leittechnik sind vorhanden und zu berücksichtigen.

title: Netherlands – Other electrical installation work – Dynamisch Verkeers Management Instandhouding (DVMI)
description: Aanleiding van de aanbesteding is de vernieuwing van de huidige vijf (5) Onderhoud DVM Wegkant (ODW) prestatiecontracten voor de beheergebieden van Rijkswaterstaat (RWS). Onder de contracten vallen assets van RWS Verkeer- en Watermanagement (hierna VWM). RWS Centrale Informatievoorziening (hierna CIV) is de eigenaar van deze ODW contracten. Deze nieuwe contracten starten afzonderlijk en eindigen op hetzelfde moment. De nieuwe contracten krijgen de naam Dynamisch Verkeers Management Instandhouding (DVMI), waarmee een verbinding is gelegd met de UAV-GCI 2019, de basisvoorwaarden voor deze contracten. Op basis van strategische afwegingen binnen RWS, is gekozen voor 1 aanbesteding met 4 percelen met ieder een nieuw Basis Onderhoud Contracten (BOC) voor onderstaande beheergebieden van RWS Perceel 1: DVMI-NWN (Noord West Nederland) Perceel 2: DVMI-NN+ON (Noord Nederland + Oost Nederland) Perceel 3: DVMI-ZN (Zuid Nederland) Perceel 4: DVMI-ZWN (Zuid West Nederland) De scope van de DVMI contracten (vier) betreft de instandhouding van het DVM areaal langs de wegkant ter bevordering van het Functioneren en Presteren van het DVM systeem. Voor een uitgebreide beschrijving van de werkzaamheden wordt verwezen naar het document Projectvisie, hoofdstuk 2.4. (Betreft bijlage A bij de Vraagspecificatie Projectmanagement)
